Expect both to change on the next deploy — 'alerting' will appear as degraded (no channel configured) and 'observability' will flip from ok to degraded until the build arg is wired. Neither is a regression; they are the new checks becoming visible.

userStories.title: Handbags and small leather goods cannot be graded — 'bag' routes into the clothing rubric
userStories.description: As a seller of handbags, I want a bag graded on the things that determine a bag's price, because 'bag' is already a garment_category and item_category has 'bags' (00230), while the only rubric that will accept it grades fabric condition at 30% and odor at 10%. A handbag's condition is corner and edge-paint wear (the single most-inspected area and the most expensive to restore), handle and strap darkening and cracking, hardware plating loss and zipper pull function, interior lining staining and pen marks and odor, structural slouch and base sag, and glazing on the edges. The category also carries the most authenticity weight of anything we touch — the existing tells (louisvuitton, coach, gucci) are ALL bag brands — so grading and the authenticity add-on land on the same item here, and the certificate has to be careful not to let a condition grade read as an authenticity verdict.
acceptanceCriteria: A handbags/leather-goods rubric is added to rubric.ts with factors, weights summing to 1.0, promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared fixture.
Photo slots cover the areas that decide a bag's grade: corners, base, interior, hardware, handles/straps, and the date-code/serial location.

A condition grade on a bag must NOT read as an authenticity statement anywhere on the certificate or in the buyer writeup — an explicit separation, test-asserted on the rendered copy, given these are the brands the authenticity add-on covers.
Measurement templates cover bag dimensions (width, height, depth, strap drop).
Prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set.
Lockstep rule holds across the three rounding sites in the same commit.
userStories.notes: [P2][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2. Highest-value of the three new-rubric stories: handbags carry the most price-per-item and are the exact brands the authenticity add-on covers (louisvuitton/coach/gucci are ALL bag brands), so the condition-vs-authenticity separation on the certificate is a liability requirement, not polish. | 2026-08-09 AC1 and AC3 DONE; AC2, AC4, AC5 and AC6 REMAIN and two of them are blocked on US-1997 Phase 2. NO MIGRATION — the rubric registry is code, and grade_reports.rubric_key/factor_scores already exist (00231). AC1: a handbags rubric is in services/edge-functions/src/lib/rubric.ts, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts, and added to src/test/fixtures/rubric-factors.json so both parity suites pin it (edge rubric-parity_test.ts 54 passed, client rubrics.test.ts 51 passed). SIX factors, one more than any existing rubric, and the shape is the argument: corners_edges 0.30, exterior 0.20, handles_straps 0.15, hardware 0.15, interior 0.10, structure 0.10. Corners and edge paint carry the most because they are the first place every buyer looks and the most expensive area to restore — a bag with perfect panels and worn corners reads as used and the reverse does not. handles_straps sits with hardware rather than under structure because its failure mode is chemical (vachetta darkening, glazing cracking) not structural. interior and structure are last because they are the two a buyer can least see in photographs, and a rubric should not weight heavily what the evidence cannot support. I ADDED AN 'exterior' FACTOR THE STORY DID NOT LIST: the AC enumerated corners, handles, hardware, interior, structure and glazing, which leaves body-panel scuffs and stains with nowhere to route — every exterior stain would have fallen through to the first factor and debited corners. defectRouting is reconciled to the real DefectType taxonomy with nothing invented, the same discipline US-1997 applied after finding seven unreachable routings; 'pilling' and 'snag_pull' are deliberately UNROUTED because they are textile failures with no leather equivalent, and they fall through to the documented first-factor rule rather than being faked into a factor they cannot physically reach. AC3 IS THE ONE THAT MATTERED MOST AND IT IS DONE, INDEPENDENTLY OF PHASE 2. Every authentication tell pack we hold is a bag brand (louisvuitton, coach, gucci), so a handbag is the single item where a condition grade and an authenticity verdict render on the same certificate — and a number beside a luxury logo reads as a verdict on the logo unless the page says otherwise. On a four-figure resale that is a liability, not a UX regret. Three places now carry the separation: the rubric's promptGuidance tells the model to say nothing about authenticity (guarding the generated WRITE-UP, which no template assertion can reach), src/pages/certificate.tsx renders it INSIDE the Factor Breakdown card, and NEW functions/_shared/condition-authenticity.ts renders it in the SSR certificate. Placement is asserted, not just presence: the notice is emitted as part of factorsHtml so it sits beside the number it qualifies — a separation in a page footer is a disclaimer nobody reaches, which is indistinguishable from not having one. The copy exists twice because a Pages Function cannot import from src/, so NEW src/test/cert-condition-authenticity.test.ts pins them string-for-string (the same remedy embed-grade-widget.test.ts uses for the AI disclosure) and asserts the notice does NOT fire for clothing/cards/watches/shoes or for a legacy certificate with no rubric_key, so existing certificates are byte-identical. 11 cases. THE SEPARATION IS KEYED ON RUBRIC, NOT ON BRAND, deliberately: keying on brand means every new luxury brand needs a code change to be covered, and the failure mode of forgetting one is silent — the certificate omits the line for the item that needed it most. REMAINING: AC2 (photo slots for corners/base/interior/hardware/handles/date-code), AC4 (measurement templates: width, height, depth, strap drop), AC5 (shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set) and AC6 (the three-rounding-site lockstep generalisation) — AC5 and AC6 are US-1997 Phase 2 and cannot be done in a sandbox: AC5 needs live traffic, real vision calls and a non-clothing golden set that does not exist, and AC6 is the variable-factor-set generalisation of the weighted overall, which US-1997 records as needing a validatable environment. AC2 and AC4 are sandbox-doable and are the next honest step. NOTE ON THE SSR CERTIFICATE, found while wiring AC3: functions/cert/[id].ts renders only the hardcoded five clothing factors and does not read rubric_key for the breakdown at all — so when Phase 2 starts writing non-clothing grades, the SSR page will show a handbag's scores against clothing labels. The separation notice IS wired there and will appear, but the factor list itself is a Phase 2 gap that nothing else records. VERIFIED: edge suite 6205 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3770 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | 2026-08-09 (second pass) AC2 DONE, AND I FIXED A BUG I SHIPPED IN THE FIRST PASS. THE BUG FIRST, because it is the more useful finding: the rubric shipped keyed 'handbags' while the item_category enum (00230) spells it 'bags'. rubricForKey() is called with an item_category, so that rubric could never have been selected — every handbag would have kept grading as clothing, which is the exact bug this story exists to fix, reintroduced by the fix. NOTHING FAILED: the rubric existed, the shared parity fixture passed, both suites were green, and the certificate rendered clothing factors. Renamed to 'bags' across rubric.ts, rubrics.ts, the fixture, the SSR shared module and the tests. THE GUARD IS THE POINT: rubric-parity_test.ts now asserts every key in RUBRICS exists in PHOTO_PROFILES, whose keys ARE the item_category vocabulary — it is the one place the edge service enumerates them. Negative-verified by renaming the key back and watching 4 cases redden. This is a DIFFERENT deadness from the import-graph kind vault/70-agent/shipped-but-unwired.md catalogues: that audit finds modules nothing imports, and this module IS imported — the dead thing was a KEY inside a lookup table, which no import graph can see. Recorded there as a generalisable rule: when reachability depends on a string matching a value declared somewhere else, pin the two together, because both halves look correct in isolation. AC2 DONE. The bags photo profile asked for front, back, brand stamp, serial, interior, one catch-all Hardware detail and extras — a set built for LISTING and AUTHENTICATING a bag, which never asked for the two areas the rubric weights most. corners_edges carries 30% of the score and had NO SLOT AT ALL, so the grader was being asked to judge corner wear from a full-front shot that physically cannot resolve it, and the seller was never told to take the photo. Three roles added, each mapped to a rubric factor: corner -> corners_edges (0.30), surface labelled 'Base' -> structure (0.10), detail_2 labelled 'Handles and Straps' -> handles_straps (0.15). Both are EXISTING storage roles from 00230, not new ones, and 'corner' already carries an 800px floor plus the 0.30 sharpness gate in macro-photo-quality.ts, so it is treated as a macro slot the moment it is offered with no further wiring. Handles use detail_2 and NOT accessory deliberately: accessory means the dust bag and the papers, and filing evidence about the ITEM under evidence about what came WITH it reads differently to the grader. Only front/back/brand-stamp stay REQUIRED — making six slots required would block a seller from advancing an item they have already photographed well enough to list, which is a different question from whether the grade will be confident, and image-quality.ts already caps confidence on a thin set. A second new guard asserts that a category with its own rubric offers a photo slot for its heaviest factor, so a future rubric cannot weight an area it never asks anyone to photograph. ALSO FIXED, an SPA-vs-SSR divergence I introduced in the first pass: the SPA keyed the authenticity separation on activeRubric.key, which only resolves to 'bags' when BOTH factor_scores and rubric_key are present (the breakdown deliberately falls back to clothing otherwise so it can render the typed columns), while the SSR page keyed it on rubric_key alone. That would have dropped the disclaimer on exactly the bag whose factor JSON did not land, while the SSR page still showed it — the failure class vault/20-domain/public-certificate-read-paths.md was written about. Both now key on rubric_key alone, which is also correct on its own terms: a bag graded off the typed columns is still a bag. Test-asserted, including that activeRubric is NOT used for it. REMAINING: AC4 (measurement templates: width, height, depth, strap drop), AC5 (shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a bootstrapped handbag golden set) and AC6 (three-rounding-site lockstep generalisation). AC5 and AC6 are US-1997 Phase 2 and need live traffic, real vision calls and a non-clothing golden set that does not exist; AC4 is sandbox-doable and is the next step. VERIFIED: edge suite 6207 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3771 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | 2026-08-09 (third pass) AC4 DONE. Only AC5 and AC6 remain, and both are US-1997 Phase 2. A new 'bag' measurement group in BOTH copies of measurement-templates.ts: width, height and depth REQUIRED, strap_drop and handle_drop optional, all on the in/cm length unit. DEPTH IS THE POINT: a 30cm tote and a 30cm clutch are different objects, and before this a bag fell through to the 'generic' group, which offers length and width and neither of them required — so the two numbers a buyer asks for first were not even offered. BOTH DROPS, not one: a top-handle bag has no strap and a crossbody has no handles, so a single shared 'strap drop' field would sit blank on half of all bags, and a blank measurement reads as 'the seller did not measure it' rather than 'this bag has no strap'. Two optional fields let the right one be filled and the wrong one be honestly empty. measurementGroupFor tests bags FIRST, before shoes, and that ordering is load-bearing: 'boot bag', 'shoe bag' and 'cargo bag' each contain a keyword a later branch claims, every one of them is a bag, and routing a boot bag to the shoe template would have asked the seller for an insole length. WIDENING THE MeasurementGroup UNION MADE THE COMPILER FIND EVERY CONSUMER, which is the argument for the union being exhaustive: four Record<MeasurementGroup, ...> maps failed to compile until each had a bag entry — fit-model.ts GROUP_DIMS, listing-templates.ts DESCRIPTION_TEMPLATES, and two in tools/fit-checker.tsx. GROUP_DIMS and both fit-checker maps are EMPTY like shoes and watches, and for the same reason: the fit engine compares a garment's flat measurements to a BODY's, and a bag has no body dimension to compare against — an entry there would have to invent one. DESCRIPTION_TEMPLATES got a real bag template rather than falling to generic, because generic leads with Size and Material and a bag has no size — its dimensions ARE its size. NEW GUARD FOR A GAP NOBODY HAD FILED: the two measurement-template files are byte-identical and NOTHING pinned them — the third instance of this shape in the repo after the rubric definitions (US-1997) and title-sync (US-1995), and the first one pinned BEFORE a divergence became possible rather than after. src/test/measurement-template-parity.test.ts asserts byte equality (correct here, unlike title-sync where the two implementations legitimately differ — these two are meant to BE the same file, so equality is the actual contract and it fails with a readable diff). The failure it prevents is quiet: measurements are stored on inventory_items.measurements keyed by the field key, so one side renaming a key means the form writes strap_drop, the extractor reads something else, and the number the seller typed simply stops arriving at the listing description, the size estimate and the MeasureCard gate. Nothing errors. 7 cases. ALSO CORRECTED A VAULT CLAIM found while re-reading the drifted note: vault/20-domain/listing-photos.md said 'since 00306, required = front + back only' as a blanket rule, and photo-profiles.ts is PER CATEGORY — bags has required 'marking' on top of front and back, and had before I touched it. The sentence describes the clothing default and the items_full.has_required_photos column, not every category; it now says so and points at requiredPhotoTypesFor(category). Also recorded there and in the code that the bags role ORDER changed (condition shots ahead of interior and the date code) with front still at index 0, so no cover image moved — roles[] drives sort_order and index 0 is the eBay cover. VERIFIED: edge suite 6207 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3778 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean.

userStories.title: Headwear cannot be graded — hats have a garment_category, no rubric, no photo slots and no measurements
userStories.description: As a seller of hats, I want to grade a cap the way I grade a hoodie, because headwear is a high-volume resale category and today 'hat' is a garment_category value that routes into a clothing rubric which cannot express it. Verified: GARMENT_CATEGORIES includes 'hat'; rubric.ts has clothing, sports_cards, watches and shoes and nothing else; MEASUREMENT_TEMPLATES has top/bottom/dress/outerwear/shoes/watch/generic and nothing else; the required image types are front/back/label. A fitted cap's condition lives in places none of those reach: brim shape and flatness, crown structure and collapse, the sweatband (the first thing to fail and the first thing a buyer inspects), the button and eyelets, embroidery integrity and pulls, and staining at the front panel and sweatband.
acceptanceCriteria: A headwear rubric is added to rubric.ts with its own factors and weights summing to 1.0, plus promptGuidance and defectRouting, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts and pinned by the shared rubric-factors fixture.
A headwear measurement template is added (fitted size / circumference, crown height, brim length) in the units the category actually uses.
Headwear-appropriate photo slots exist (crown, brim, sweatband/interior, label) — grading a cap from front/back/label alone cannot see the sweatband, which is where the wear is.
The weighted-overall computation stays in lockstep across all three rounding sites in the same commit as any factor-set generalization this requires.

The new rubric's prompts go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary against a headwear golden set that must be bootstrapped first — a rubric with no golden set cannot pass the gate and must not be activated around it.
Any enum widening (image_type, garment_category) follows the US-1108 triple and the enum caveats in the migrations skill.
userStories.notes: [P3][Grading/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Depends on US-1997 Phase 2 — the factor-set generalization across the three lockstep rounding sites is a prerequisite for ANY new rubric, and US-1997's notes already scope it. Do not build a fourth rubric before that lands. | 2026-08-09 AC1, AC2 and AC3 DONE; AC6 DEFERRED; AC4 and AC5 remain and are US-1997 Phase 2. NO MIGRATION, deliberately — see AC6. AC1: a HEADWEAR rubric in rubric.ts, mirrored in src/lib/rubrics.ts, pinned by the shared fixture. crown_structure 0.25, brim 0.25, sweatband 0.20, fabric_graphics 0.20, hardware_closure 0.10. THE WEIGHTS SPLIT INTO TWO QUESTIONS and that is the design: brim + crown together are half the score because together they answer 'is this still a hat' — a collapsed crown or a cracked brim insert is not recoverable and the cap is worth its logo and nothing else. sweatband and fabric answer 'will someone wear it', which is the other half of a resale decision and not the same question. THE STORY ARGUES FOR SWEATBAND FIRST and it is 0.20; the reason is worth reading rather than assuming I under-weighted it. It is the most COMMON failure, not the most terminal one. A stained sweatband is close to permanent and will lose a sale, so it carries real weight — but a cap with a perfect crown and brim and a grim sweatband is still a cap, while the reverse is not. defectRouting is reconciled to the real DefectType taxonomy with nothing invented: seam_failure_unthreading splits sweatband/crown (the band separating from the crown is the canonical case), stretched_misshapen goes to crown+brim (a collapsed crown, a brim that lost its curve), odor_indicator wholly to sweatband. 'stain' is split 0.6 sweatband / 0.4 fabric rather than routed wholly to the band — salt lines are the common case, but a mark on a white front panel is the other place a cap dies. promptGuidance carries the intentional-vs-wear line the block exists for: a flat brim on a flat-brim cap and a curved brim on a curved-brim cap are BOTH as-made, and factory distressing on a vintage-styled cap is design. AC3: a headwear photo profile. The story's own sentence is the requirement — 'grading a cap from front/back/label alone cannot see the sweatband, which is where the wear is' — so 'interior' IS the sweatband shot, relabelled 'Sweatband' with the hint 'turn it over', because 'Interior' alone does not tell a seller to photograph the one thing a buyer checks first. I did NOT invent a 'sweatband' storage type: that would need an image_type enum migration for a photo the existing role already describes. 'angle' carries crown and brim together in one three-quarter view, since both are heaviest and both read badly from a flat front. The rubric-parity guard now requires BOTH slots for headwear, so this cannot regress. AC2: a headwear measurement group in both copies. circumference REQUIRED, crown_height and brim_length optional, all as LENGTHS. That is the decision: a fitted cap's '7 3/8' is a size LABEL nobody put a tape to and belongs in the item's size field, and half of resale headwear is snapback or strapback with no numeric size at all — a size-only template would leave those unmeasurable. Routing tests headwear before accessories so 'bucket hat' is not claimed elsewhere, and after bags so a 'hat bag' stays a bag; 'visor' is included because it is a brim and a band and nothing else, which this template covers exactly. ⚠ THE RUBRIC AND PROFILE ARE INERT TODAY, and this is recorded IN THE CODE as well as here because a future reader finds the rubric before the note: both are keyed by item_category and the enum has no 'headwear' value, so rubricForKey() can never select it — the same inert-until-activated state the non-clothing rubrics have had since US-1997. AC6 DEFERRED, and it is an operational call rather than a technical one, identical to US-2224's AC3: the enum widening is small and additive, but SIX migrations (00564-00569) are already held and unapplied to prod, two with strict apply-before-push ordering, and adding more to an unapplied queue raises the cost and risk of the eventual apply session. US-2223 AC6 and US-2224 AC3 should ship as ONE migration in the next batch — both widen the same taxonomy (headwear, neckwear, gloves) and splitting them across two files buys nothing. AC4 (three-rounding-site lockstep across a variable factor set) and AC5 (shadow -> eval -> canary against a headwear golden set that must be bootstrapped first) are US-1997 Phase 2 and need live traffic, real vision calls and correction data that does not exist. VERIFIED: edge suite 6209 passed / 0 failed, deno lint + check clean, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3795 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | 2026-08-09 (second pass) AC6 DONE. Migration 00570_headwear_neckwear_gloves_categories.sql adds item_category 'headwear' (plus the two garment_category values US-2224 AC3 needs — ONE migration for both stories, because they widen the same taxonomy for the same reason and splitting them would mean two apply steps, two rollbacks and two chances to apply one without the other). US-1108 triple complete: idempotent ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS, EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION bumped to 00570 in the same commit, self-record footer, manifest regenerated. WHY HEADWEAR IS ITS OWN TOP LEVEL rather than folded under 'accessories', recorded in the migration itself because a future reader will find the SQL before the story: item_category is the dimension that selects the grading rubric AND the photo profile AND the measurement template. A cap's condition lives in the crown, the brim and the sweatband; an accessory's lives in its material, edges and hardware. Filing headwear under accessories would have left the headwear rubric permanently unreachable while looking correct — the same silent deadness rubric-parity_test.ts was written to catch, and the exact bug I shipped and fixed on the bags rubric earlier today. NO TRANSACTION WRAPPER, deliberately: Postgres refuses to USE a new enum value in the transaction that adds it, and although nothing here uses one, wrapping it would make the file unsafe for the next person to extend. THE FRONTEND MIRRORS ARE UPDATED IN THE SAME COMMIT, which is what makes this PUSH-BLOCKING: ITEM_CATEGORIES and GARMENT_CATEGORIES in src/lib/constants.ts and the GarmentCategory union in src/types/database.ts now carry the new values and drive pickers that write straight to the database under RLS — so if Pages deploys before the SQL applies, a seller who picks 'Hats & caps' gets an invalid-enum error and the save fails. PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md says so, and also records that the ROLLBACK IS NOT CLEAN: Postgres cannot drop an enum value, so reverting means recreating the type and rewriting every column that uses it — in practice you leave the values (inert until written) and roll the frontend back. VERIFIED: node scripts/verify.mjs --db re-applied every migration from zero on a throwaway stack, npx tsc -b clean, npm run lint 0 errors, ui:check 0 blocking, web suite 3807 passed / 0 failed, edge suite 6213 passed / 0 failed including rubric-parity and schema-version. REMAINING on this story: AC4 and AC5 only, both US-1997 Phase 2 (the three-rounding-site lockstep generalisation, and shadow -> eval -> canary against a headwear golden set that must be bootstrapped from real corrections first). | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (second half of the day): the HELD-migration claim in this story's notes is now STALE. Migrations 00564, 00569 and 00570 are on origin/main - verified with git ls-tree against a freshly fetched origin/main, not inferred - and the branch has zero unpushed commits. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: pushed is not applied. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose. Recorded because prd-lint caught it the same hour the branch moved, which is the guard working as intended - it went unactioned for weeks before, and a stale freeze cost real sessions.

userStories.title: Edge builds ship with release="dev" — every prod edge error is unattributable to a commit (frontend is correct)
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want to know which build produced a production error. The frontend does: https://gradethread.com serves a bundle tagged release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814", a real commit SHA, so Cloudflare Pages is wiring VITE_RELEASE_SHA correctly. The EDGE does not: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health returns {"env":"production","release":"dev"}, measured 2026-07-18. Root cause is exact — services/edge-functions/Dockerfile:12 declares ARG GIT_SHA=dev and line 13 sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA}; its own comment (lines 9-11) says the builder must pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT, and the Coolify build is not doing so, so the literal default ships. lib/observability.ts:52 releaseSha() therefore returns "dev" and tags every Sentry event, structured log and trace with it. This is an ASYMMETRY between the two halves of the system, and the half that is blind is the one handling grading, payments, eBay writes and webhooks.
acceptanceCriteria: The Coolify build passes the commit into the image (GIT_SHA build arg = $SOURCE_COMMIT or the platform equivalent), so RELEASE_SHA is a real SHA in production.
GET /health on production returns a release that matches the deployed commit — verify by measuring the endpoint after a deploy, not by reading the config.
Sentry edge events carry that release, so an error can be attributed to a deploy and "did the fix ship?" is answerable. Confirm a real event is tagged.

A guard so this cannot silently regress: the edge should REFUSE to report healthy-and-production while release is the literal default "dev"/"unknown" — or at minimum surface it as a degraded feature in /health/ready features{} alongside the existing observability entry, which currently reports "ok" while the release is meaningless.
Document the build-arg requirement in COOLIFY.md next to the other deploy settings, since the Dockerfile comment alone did not survive contact with the actual deploy.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Ops/Observability][Measured] Found 2026-07-18 during the cross-platform production-readiness deep dive, by querying prod rather than reading config. EVIDENCE, all live: /health -> {"status":"ok","service":"gradethread-edge-functions","env":"production","release":"dev","errorTracking":"enabled"}; the frontend bundle /assets/index-CIbHzx5V.js contains release:"c9631342084bfd9e96883321a07a390d3be1e814" (which is also proof Pages auto-deployed that commit). WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A COSMETIC TAG: with every edge event tagged "dev" you cannot (a) attribute a production error to a build, (b) tell whether a deployed fix actually shipped, (c) see a regression appear at a release boundary, or (d) make a rollback decision on evidence — and ROLLBACK.md assumes you can identify the bad build. Note errorTracking reports "enabled" and /health/ready features.observability reports "ok", so the health surface actively says observability is fine while the release dimension of it is inert; that is why AC4 asks for a guard rather than just a config fix. The fix itself is small (one build arg); the reason it survived this long is that nothing measured it. | 2026-07-19 AC1/AC4/AC5 DONE; AC2/AC3 need a deploy to confirm. THE ROOT CAUSE WAS A MISSING BUILD ARG, and the fix is DECLARATIVE rather than another instruction: docker-compose.coolify.yml now carries build.args GIT_SHA: dev. That placement is the whole point — the Dockerfile has carried a comment telling the builder to pass GIT_SHA since it was written, and per this story's own evidence that comment did not survive contact with the actual deploy. A build arg in compose is APPLIED BY THE PLATFORM instead of remembered by a person, so documenting it harder would have reproduced the same failure. The :-dev fallback keeps a plain local docker compose build working. AC4 DONE and it is the anti-regression half: the observability feature group now requires SENTRY_DSN *and* a real RELEASE_SHA, so /health/ready reports observability DEGRADED while the release is a placeholder — previously it reported 'ok' in the exact prod state this story measured (errorTracking enabled, release 'dev'), which is the false confidence that let it sit unnoticed. isRealReleaseSha is deliberately permissive on FORM: it rejects the placeholder set (dev/unknown/local/none/latest/empty) but accepts short SHAs and tags, because the measured failure was the literal ARG default surviving the build, not a malformed SHA — requiring 40 hex chars would break tag-based deploys for no benefit. 4 tests, including the exact prod state as a case. AC5 DONE in COOLIFY.md with a MEASURE-DO-NOT-READ verification step (curl /health | jq .release), plus the warning that deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant needs the same args block. ⚠ REMAINING AND GENUINELY UNVERIFIABLE FROM HERE: AC2 (measure /health after a deploy) and AC3 (confirm a real Sentry event carries the release). Both require the deploy to actually happen. What HAS changed is that a regression now announces itself on /health/ready instead of waiting for someone to think to curl. [2026-07-19 AC4+AC5 DONE, AC1-AC3 NEED THE COOLIFY BUILD + A PROD MEASUREMENT] AC4: /health/ready now carries features.release, degraded whenever the release is unattributable (dev / unknown / empty / whitespace, case-insensitive). Deliberately a SEPARATE key from features.observability: that group reports ok whenever a Sentry DSN is present, which stays true and stays misleading while every event it ships is tagged dev. Also deliberately does NOT flip the service to not_ready — the AC allowed either, and refusing readiness on an untagged build would pull grading, payments and webhooks out of rotation to protect observability. health.ts already argues this exact principle for the schema probe (a probe that can fail a container over a diagnostic is a worse bug than the blind spot it fixes). A test asserts ready stays true. releaseReadiness() is pure; 5 new tests. AC5 FINDING: COOLIFY.md already had a US-2001 build-args section from an earlier pass, and it CLAIMED /health/ready reports features.observability as degraded on a placeholder release. That was FALSE — nothing implemented it. The documentation described a guard that did not exist, which is a plausible reason nobody built one; same defect class as US-2035 (comment asserting a property the code lacks) and US-2123 (copy advertising an ungranted entitlement). Doc now names the real key, shows the curl, and records the correction rather than quietly overwriting it. STILL OPEN (all need the deploy, not code): AC1 the Coolify build must actually pass GIT_SHA=$SOURCE_COMMIT — docker-compose.coolify.yml declares it but prod measured release=dev on 2026-07-18, so either the deploy uses docker-compose.yml or the Build Args field is unset. AC2 verify by curling /health after a deploy. AC3 confirm a real Sentry event carries the SHA. The new features.release entry makes AC2 checkable without remembering the curl. | 2026-08-02 AC2 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and it FAILS. The AC insisted on measuring the endpoint rather than reading the config, and that instruction earned its keep: GET https://functions.gradethread.com/health/ready returns features.release = 'unattributable: release="dev" — the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg, so errors cannot be tied to a commit'. So AC1 is declared but NOT IN EFFECT. docker-compose.coolify.yml carries build.args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, and the running image was still built without it. Three candidate causes, in the order worth checking: (1) Coolify is deploying from docker-compose.yml rather than the .coolify.yml variant — the previous pass explicitly warned that the plain file needs the same args block, and that warning is now the leading hypothesis rather than a footnote; (2) the running image predates the compose change and no rebuild has happened since; (3) SOURCE_COMMIT is not populated in this Coolify version, so the :-dev fallback wins silently — which is exactly what the fallback is designed to do and exactly why it is indistinguishable from cause (2) without a rebuild. AC3 (a real Sentry event carrying the release) is moot until this is fixed: every event currently ships tagged 'dev', which is the state the story exists to end. WHAT THIS CONFIRMS ABOUT AC4, and it is the useful part: the guard works. /health/ready reported the problem in plain language, unprompted, to a caller who did nothing but curl a public endpoint. That is the difference between a config that is wrong and a config that ANNOUNCES it is wrong — before this, the only way to learn it was to notice that every Sentry release said dev. The AC4 decision not to flip the service to not_ready also holds up: the service is genuinely serving, and pulling grading and payments out of rotation to protect observability would have been the wrong trade. STILL OPEN: AC1 in practice (the build arg must actually reach the image), AC2 re-measured after that deploy, AC3 confirmed on a real event. All three need one Coolify rebuild, and the first thing to check is which compose file the service is deploying from. ALSO OBSERVED IN THE SAME RESPONSE, recorded here because it is the same curl: schema reports {expected:00512, applied:00512, status:match}. See the note on the held-migration gate. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-03: any "HELD"/"apply-BEFORE-push" wording earlier in this note describes the state AT THE TIME OF WRITING and is STALE. Prod was measured at applied=00514 on 2026-08-03 via /health/ready (the database's own answer, not a recollection), and every migration up to 00514 is on origin/main. The only migration currently held is 00515 (US-2168), which is unrelated to this story. Do not read this note as evidence that the branch is frozen. | 2026-08-08 CAUSE (1) CONFIRMED AND FIXED. The 2026-08-02 pass listed three candidate causes and said the first thing to check is which compose file the service deploys from. Checked it, and the answer is in this repo's own doc: COOLIFY.md line 11 says the one-time setup makes Coolify 'auto-pick docker-compose.yml'. That file's first line calls itself 'Production compose used by Coolify' — and it had NO build.args block. So the arg was declared only in docker-compose.coolify.yml, which is not the file the documented setup deploys. docker-compose.staging.yml was missing it too.

FIX: both now declare args.GIT_SHA: ${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}, identical to the .coolify.yml one. Deliberately declared in ALL of them rather than picking the 'right' one — the question 'which compose file is it actually using?' is precisely what nobody could answer for three weeks, and making the answer irrelevant is cheaper than making it knowable.

NEW STATIC GUARD (AC4's missing half): services/edge-functions/src/tests/compose-release-arg_test.ts walks every docker-compose*.yml, and any file with a build: section that lacks GIT_SHA fails CI with the reason. It also asserts the Dockerfile still wires ARG GIT_SHA -> ENV RELEASE_SHA, so the guard cannot stay green over a dead mechanism. Override files with no build: section (docker-compose.dev.yml) are exempt — they inherit the base build. Sabotage-verified: deleted the arg line from docker-compose.yml, test failed naming the file; restored, 2 passed. deno lint + deno check clean.

WHY A STATIC GUARD ON TOP OF THE RUNTIME ONE: the /health/ready guard worked exactly as designed and still cost three weeks, because it can only speak after a bad image is already serving. A per-file declaration that only one file carries is a per-file bug, and nothing was looking ACROSS the files. This test looks across the files.

COOLIFY.md rewritten: the old text carried a warning telling the operator to add the block by hand or fill in Coolify's Build Args field — asking a person to remember something, which is the failure mode this story is about, and the Dockerfile had been asking in a comment since it was written. It now states all three files declare it, records why, and keeps ONE residual manual step for the only cause the code cannot rule out (a Coolify version that does not populate SOURCE_COMMIT, where :-dev wins silently).

STILL passes:false, and only on the deploy: AC2 (curl /health/ready after a Coolify rebuild and see a real SHA) and AC3 (confirm a Sentry event carries it). Both need a rebuild, which ADE Hub is disarmed for. Nothing further is doable from a checkout — the code side of AC1 is now complete on all three files and guarded. | 2026-08-09 A SECOND, INDEPENDENT FAULT FOUND — the build arg was never the whole story, and every prior pass (incl. mine) chased it alone. MEASURED FIRST: GET /health returned release:"dev" on an image whose SAME response reported schema.expected=00585, i.e. an image built AFTER the 2026-08-08 commit that put build.args.GIT_SHA in all three compose files. That eliminates the 2026-08-02 note's cause (2) 'the running image predates the compose change'. THE CODE BUG: observability.ts releaseSha() read RELEASE_SHA ?? COMMIT_SHA ?? SOURCE_COMMIT ?? GIT_SHA, and its comment claimed it 'accepts any of the common env names so the same code works on Coolify / CI / local'. It does not. Dockerfile sets ENV RELEASE_SHA=${GIT_SHA} with ARG GIT_SHA=dev, so RELEASE_SHA is ALWAYS SET in the image — to the literal 'dev'. ?? falls through on undefined, never on a placeholder VALUE, so the first key always won and the other three were DEAD CODE on the only platform they were written for. Consequence that matters most: setting SOURCE_COMMIT by hand in Coolify — the obvious workaround, and the one COOLIFY.md was steering toward — would have been SILENTLY IGNORED. FIXED: new services/edge-functions/src/lib/release-identity.ts (resolveRelease/isPlaceholderRelease/RELEASE_ENV_KEYS) falls through placeholder VALUES; observability.ts, env-validation.ts isRealReleaseSha and routes/health.ts all consolidated onto it — health.ts had its OWN narrower set ['dev','unknown',''] so /health/ready could have called a release of 'local' ok while env-validation called it a placeholder. Two more instances of the same defect class fixed: (a) agent-tools.ts:654 releaseSha() fed US-1610's release-verify agent, which detects a deploy by watching that value CHANGE — a constant 'dev' is not an error, it is a value that never changes, so that agent has reported 'no deploy' on every run since it shipped; it now returns null on a placeholder so no-identity stays distinguishable from an identity. (b) releaseReadiness()'s message asserted the cause ('the image was built without a GIT_SHA build arg') and was measured saying so on an image that HAD the arg — it now states the symptom and names the keys checked. RUNTIME ROUTE ADDED: all three compose files pass SOURCE_COMMIT + COMMIT_SHA through as BARE environment entries (no '='), deliberately — a runtime env var overrides the image ENV, so the safer-looking '- SOURCE_COMMIT=${SOURCE_COMMIT:-dev}' would clobber a correctly stamped image whenever the host lacks the var. So setting SOURCE_COMMIT in Coolify now fixes prod WITHOUT a rebuild, which is the fastest thing to try. VERIFIED BY SABOTAGE, 5/5: restoring the original ??-chain, dropping the runtime pass-through, writing it in the clobbering '=' form, narrowing the placeholder set, and reverting isRealReleaseSha to read RELEASE_SHA alone each redden a named test. ⚠ THE FIFTH SURVIVED AT FIRST — no test covered the disagreement case (health says unattributable while Sentry events are correctly tagged), which is exactly the state that would send someone to fix a build arg that already works. Added that case. Full edge suite 6359 passed / 0 failed; deno lint + deno check clean; web tsc -b + eslint clean. DOCS: COOLIFY.md now records that the build arg was insufficient and gives the no-rebuild fix first. vault/10-ops/rollback.md gained a warning that GET /health cannot currently identify the running build, which that runbook's step 3 depends on — identify it from Coolify's deployment history instead; the same caveat is in the admin rollback runbook (src/lib/admin/runbooks.ts) since that is what gets read mid-incident. vault/10-ops/env-reference.md now documents the precedence and the placeholder fall-through. STILL passes:false on AC2/AC3, unchanged: both need a deploy or an env-var change on the Coolify side, then re-measure /health. What changed is that the fix no longer requires a rebuild.

userStories.title: Category grading criteria cover 8 of 20 garment categories — 12 categories grade with no category guidance at all
userStories.description: As a seller of a shirt, a coat or a skirt, I want the grader to know what matters on my category, because the ones that do get it are measurably better guided. Verified: ai-grading.ts:320 GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA has exactly 8 keys (jeans, pants, shorts, jacket, sweater, hoodie, t-shirt, dress) while src/lib/constants.ts GARMENT_CATEGORIES has 20 values. The 12 with no entry — shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf, other — fall through to the generic prompt with only DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE. Each of the missing ones has real category-specific signal the model is currently not told to look for: collar and cuff fray and yellowing on shirts, seam slippage and pulls on blouses, lining and shell separation and pilling on wool coats, zipper and hem and lining on skirts, and for footwear the outsole and midsole entirely.
acceptanceCriteria: Every value in GARMENT_CATEGORIES has a criteria entry, or the fallback is made explicit and deliberate for the ones that genuinely have none.
Each new entry follows the existing voice: what is INTENTIONAL design on this category vs what is genuine wear, since that distinction is the whole point of the block.
The prompt change ships as a new prompt version through shadow -> golden-set eval gate -> canary, not a silent edit — this changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once.
Golden-set cases exist for the newly-covered categories before activation, tagged so the eval report can slice per category.
Categories already covered produce byte-identical prompts, test-guarded, so the eval measures only the new coverage.
userStories.notes:

Cheapest coverage win in the epic (prompt data, no schema), but it changes the per-image prompt for 12 categories at once so it needs a real eval cycle and per-category golden cases first. | 2026-08-08 AC1/AC2/AC5 DONE. AC3 IS NOT IMPLEMENTABLE AS WRITTEN, and that is the finding. AC4 unchanged and still blocking.

AC1: all 11 remaining categories written (shirt, blouse, coat, skirt, sneakers, boots, sandals, hat, bag, belt, scarf). "other" is DELIBERATELY left uncovered and the absence is now pinned by a test: it is the value assigned when the category is UNKNOWN (garment-mapping.ts maps five of six garment types to it), so an "other" item may be any of the twenty and there is no honest guidance to give. Generic filler there would restate DESIGN_VS_DEFECT_PRINCIPLE and make coverage look complete while the real gap is upstream classification.

AC2: each entry draws the design-vs-defect line, and a test fails any entry that names only defects. The calls worth having are the ones a generic prompt gets backwards: midsole yellowing on sneakers is OXIDATION not soil (and some releases ship pre-yellowed), vachetta patina on a bag is supposed to darken, leather patina on boots is desirable aging, the molded footbed impression on sandals is permanent use that affects resale, and the fold crease at the worn hole is the defining signal on a belt.

AC3 CANNOT BE SATISFIED — verified, not assumed. The AC says ship through shadow -> golden-set eval -> canary. That lifecycle covers the SYSTEM prompt ONLY. GARMENT_CATEGORY_CRITERIA is interpolated into the per-image USER message by buildUserPrompt, and: an ai_prompt_versions row carries one prompt_text which becomes the system block, so no override can reach it; canary picks between two system texts; runEval overrides system text only, so the criteria are ambient on BOTH legs of its comparison; grading-shadow.ts is composite-stage only AND reuses per-image results verbatim, so there is no per-image shadow path at all. Worse, PerImageAnalysis carries no version field, so PER_IMAGE_PROMPT_VERSION never reaches a grade record — bumping it would have looked like compliance and changed nothing.

So the change ships ENV-FLAG GATED (GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2, default OFF), which is the only gate the architecture offers and is the same pattern GRADING_BASELINES / GRADING_TAG_OCR already use. The eleven entries live in a SEPARATE map from the shipped eight, so byte-identity is a property of the file rather than a claim a reviewer has to diff. Composite grades attributed with a +cat2 suffix, appended last per the stated ordering rule.

AC5 DONE and strengthened: byte-identical for the eight with the gate ON, AND a no-op for all twenty with it OFF, so deploying this commit changes no grade. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED four ways — dropped a category entry (AC1 + coverage + disjoint reddened), flipped the gate to default-on (the no-op test reddened), duplicated a key into both maps (only the source-scan caught it, which is exactly why that test is a source scan and not behavioural), and moved +cat2 out of last position (ordering test reddened).

STILL passes:false: AC4 (golden-set cases for the newly-covered categories, tagged for per-category slicing) needs real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet — the same bootstrap problem US-1997 Phase 2 has. Until then the flag stays off, and the flag being off is why that is safe rather than merely convenient. The structural fix for AC3 is US-2432.

That fix shipped as US-2438: category_criteria is now one of two blocks in a versioned registry (ai_prompt_block_versions, migration 00563), and runEval takes a blockCandidate that pins exactly that block while the system prompt stays active. So the eval-gate leg of AC3 is available today. And AC4 is unchanged and still blocking on its own: a per-category golden set has to come from real human-corrected grades on those categories, which do not exist yet. So GRADING_CATEGORY_CRITERIA_V2 stays OFF and this story stays passes:false — what changed is that the gate is now buildable rather than architecturally unreachable. | 2026-08-09 CORRECTION: THE SHADOW BLOCKER NAMED IN THE NOTE ABOVE IS GONE. userStories.title: Backups: mechanism verified, prod backup cron never installed — real RPO is total loss
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want prod data to be recoverable. The scripts are all real and executable (scripts/ops/backup-postgres.sh, backup-storage.sh, restore-postgres.sh, restore-drill.sh) and a restore drill genuinely passed 2026-06-12 (BACKUPS.md:129, 270 RLS policies matched) — but that drill ran against a LOCAL stack at migration 00151. The prod side is unchecked: LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:236-243 has all five boxes unticked, including 'Backup cron installed on the DB host' and 'first nightly dump confirmed in the offsite bucket'; the drill table at :231-234 is empty. PITR is explicitly aspirational (BACKUPS.md:90-92, 'MANUAL: wal-g setup happens on the prod host'). So the documented RPO<=24h / RTO<=2h is only true if a cron nobody confirmed is running. Prod is a SINGLE-NODE self-hosted Postgres (SCALING.md:47) holding grades, billing and the credit ledger.
acceptanceCriteria: Install the backup cron on the prod DB host (BACKUPS.md:42-43) and CONFIRM a dump plus its .sha256 lands in the offsite bucket — verified by listing the bucket, not by reading the runbook.

Run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:231. The 11-second figure at BACKUPS.md:129 came from a near-empty schema-only DB and will not predict prod RTO.
Either stand up wal-g PITR or amend the stated RPO to the honest nightly-dump figure — do not leave a documented RPO the infrastructure cannot deliver.
Tick the five LAUNCH_CHECKLIST boxes only once each is independently verified.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/DR][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. This is the single highest-value hour of work in the repo: the ONLY finding in the entire audit whose failure mode is unrecoverable data loss. Everything else degrades; this one ends the company. Note the shape — NOT a missing-mechanism finding. The scripts exist, they work, someone drilled them. It is an ACTIVATION gap: a runbook step marked MANUAL that was never performed, and a checklist that honestly records it was never performed. The danger is that the presence of good tooling reads as protection. | 2026-08-02 AC3's DOCUMENTATION HALF DONE — the runbook no longer states an RPO the infrastructure may not deliver. AC3 says "either stand up wal-g PITR or amend the stated RPO to the honest figure — do not leave a documented RPO the infrastructure cannot deliver." The note was already honest about ONE gap (nightly-dump 24h vs PITR 5min, with a callout saying the 24h figure stands until wal-g is configured) and blind to the bigger one: EVERY number in that Targets section is a property of the backup MECHANISM, and the mechanism running is what was never verified. If the cron is not installed on the prod host, the real RPO is not 24 hours, it is TOTAL LOSS — and the table would have told an operator otherwise at exactly the moment being wrong costs the most. Added a danger callout under Targets stating that, marked LAUNCH BLOCKER, with the two checks that settle it (crontab -l on the DB host should list the backup line from the Setup section; the offsite bucket should hold a dump from the last 24h WITH its .sha256 beside it — a dump with no checksum is a backup nobody has proven readable) and an instruction to replace the callout with the date once both are true. I did NOT assert the cron is missing. I cannot see the prod host, and a runbook that states an unverified fact as fact is the same defect one level down. It says UNVERIFIED and how to verify. WHY THIS WAS WORTH DOING WHILE THE REST IS BLOCKED: AC1, AC2 and AC4 all need someone on the prod host and are genuinely operator work. AC3 is the only half that is a claim rather than an action, and a runbook is read during an incident by someone who will not re-derive it — which is precisely when an overstated recovery point does its damage. The shape is worth remembering and is written into the callout: this is not a missing mechanism. The scripts exist, they work, the restore was drilled on 2026-06-12. It is a runbook step marked MANUAL that nobody performed. STILL OPEN, all operator: install the cron and confirm a dump plus checksum lands offsite (AC1), run restore-postgres.sh against a REAL offsite dump on a scratch host and record the measured timing (AC2), tick the five launch-checklist boxes only once each is independently verified (AC4).

userStories.title: Every alert channel is optional and silently no-ops — nothing proves anyone gets paged
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want a SEV1 to reach a human. Today every channel degrades to silence when unconfigured. .github/workflows/uptime.yml:46 marks UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK 'Optional' and scripts/ops/uptime-check.mjs:188 logs 'not set — skipping webhook channel' then continues. Edge-side, ops-events.ts:104-108 falls back to MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, which ENV_REFERENCE.md:168 marks as not set. ops-events.ts:242-244 records an ops_event.alert_undelivered metric when neither channel exists — a metric that itself has no alert. INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:42-46 asserts all three sources 'must point at the same on-call channel before launch', which is an instruction, not a verified state; LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264-268 leaves it unchecked. The only channel that works with zero config is the GitHub uptime issue fallback, which pages only if repo-watch mobile notifications happen to be on.
acceptanceCriteria: Set UPTIME_ALERT_WEBHOOK and MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK, then RUN THE DRILL: break a target, confirm the message arrives on a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md. Configuration is not evidence.

Make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric — fail at boot (or emit at critical) when production has no alert channel configured. A monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence.
Confirm Sentry alert routing actually delivers (LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md:264) — see also the webhook dead-letter story, which routes ONLY to Sentry.
Measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target in INCIDENT_RESPONSE.md:33 — a 10-minute GitHub cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified.
userStories.notes: [P1][Ops/Alerting][LAUNCH BLOCKER] Found 2026-07-18 by the operational-readiness deep dive. Pairs with the backup story: that one is about surviving a disaster, this one is about LEARNING there is one. Every other alerting improvement is worthless until these two secrets are set and drilled, because they are the last mile for all of them. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (partially — see below); AC1/AC3/AC4 still need you. AC2 asked to make alert_undelivered loud rather than a silent metric, because 'a monitoring system that cannot page is worse than none, because it produces false confidence'. Added an 'alerting' feature group to env-validation: in PRODUCTION ONLY, a deploy with none of MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL set now reports DEGRADED on /health/ready and warns at boot, instead of the current state where every channel silently no-ops and nothing says so. Non-production is exempt via enabledWhen — a dev box has no business paging anyone, and warning there would train people to ignore the warning. ANY channel satisfies it, deliberately: the failure being caught is 'none of them', not 'not the one I expected'. I did NOT make it fatal at boot, which AC2 offered as an option. Refusing to start the edge because no webhook is configured would convert a monitoring gap into a total outage — strictly worse than the problem, and the opposite of the fail-open reasoning applied in US-2013. Degraded-and-loud is the right severity for 'we cannot tell you when things break'. STILL BLOCKED ON YOU and this is the launch-blocker part: AC1 (set the two secrets, break a target, confirm the message reaches a phone, record the date in LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers) and AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target). Configuration is not evidence and neither is a degraded-flag — this story stays open until a human has watched an alert arrive. Note US-2004's cron stall detector is now proven to detect, so it is queued up behind exactly this last mile. | 2026-08-02 MEASURED AGAINST PRODUCTION, and fixed a reporting bug the measurement exposed. AC2's health surface WORKS: GET /health/ready reports features.alerting = "ok", so at least one channel (MONITOR_ALERT_WEBHOOK / MONITOR_ALERT_EMAIL / SMTP_ADMIN_EMAIL) IS configured in prod. That is worth recording plainly, because AC1's framing assumed none were set. What is still unproven is whether a message actually ARRIVES — AC1's drill is about delivery, not configuration, and a configured webhook pointing at a dead endpoint reports "ok" here forever. THE BUG THE SAME CURL FOUND: features.observability returned the literal string "missing: " — nothing after the colon. The cause is a group whose satisfiedWhen fails while every var it LISTS is present. observability requires SENTRY_DSN plus a real RELEASE_SHA; the DSN is set, so the `miss` array is empty, and the message named nothing. An operator reading that at 3am is told something is missing and refused the name of it, which is worse than no line at all because it costs them the time to go looking. FIXED in computeFeatureReadiness and warnMissingFeatureGroups: when nothing is literally absent, the message now says the vars are all present and the check still rejected one, instead of an empty list. Two tests pin both paths — the all-present case, and the regression that a genuinely absent var must still be NAMED, which is the whole value of the line for every other group. WORTH BEING PRECISE ABOUT WHAT observability's DEGRADED MEANS, since "missing" read alarmingly and I nearly reported it that way: Sentry IS configured and IS receiving events. The group is degraded solely because RELEASE_SHA is "dev" — US-2001's problem, reported here as a second symptom. So the dead-letter path in US-2011 does reach Sentry; its events are simply untagged and unattributable to a commit. One Coolify rebuild with the GIT_SHA build arg clears BOTH this line and US-2001. STILL OPEN AND ALL OPERATOR WORK: AC1's drill (break a target, confirm the page lands on a phone, date it in the launch checklist), AC3 (confirm Sentry routing delivers — see US-2011, which routes ONLY to Sentry), AC4 (measure detection latency against the 15-minute ack target; a 10-minute cron plus jitter can consume most of it before a human is notified). None is a code change and none can be done from a checkout. VERIFIED: edge suite 5092 passed / 0 failed, deno lint clean across 1291 files.

userStories.title: eBay Media API: video upload for listings
userStories.description: As a clothing seller, I want to add video to my listings to lift conversion. Today images are passed as external URLs only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls) and there is no video support. Integrate the eBay Media API (/commerce/media) to upload video and attach it to listings.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge can createVideo -> uploadVideo -> poll getVideo to a terminal status, and attach the resulting id via product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem

TRANSCODE DECISION MADE AND WRITTEN DOWN: eBay accepts .mp4 H.264/AVC only, and iPhones record HEVC by default. Either the client transcodes before upload, or the edge does, or HEVC is rejected with a message that tells the seller how to fix it. Silently failing on the most common input is not an option

PUBLISH-ORDERING DECISION MADE: processing is async and terminal status is not immediate, so either publish waits for LIVE, or publish proceeds without video and a later revise attaches it. Whichever is chosen, a seller never ends up with a listing that permanently lacks the video they added
BLOCKED is handled as a moderation outcome, not an error: it is terminal and expected, and the seller is told their video was rejected rather than shown a retry that cannot succeed
Video upload gets its own validation path. The US-276 hardening (validateImageUpload / stripImageMetadata) is image-only and does NOT cover video, which also carries GPS/EXIF-equivalent metadata
iOS/web can add a video during compose and see it reflected on the published listing
Respects the Media API POST rate limit (50 requests / 5 seconds, per user)
userStories.notes:
[P3][Edge/Media] iOS listing-lifecycle audit 2026-07-14. No Media API; images external-URL only (InventoryItemPayload.imageUrls). Nice-to-have; video is a real apparel conversion lever. 

INVESTIGATED 2026-07-18. Confirmed greenfield: no videoId / commerce-media / uploadVideo reference anywhere in services/edge-functions/src or src. Two findings change the shape of this story.

FINDING 1 — NOT SCOPE-BLOCKED, contrary to the obvious assumption. The Media API's createVideo requires sell.inventory, which is ALREADY in our production grant (ebay-client.ts:233). This story therefore does NOT depend on US-1421 (restricted-scope acquisition) and does not need a new seller consent round. Attachment is also on the path we already use: product.videoIds on createOrReplaceInventoryItem — a sibling of the product.imageUrls we already send at ebay-client.ts:2163 — NOT a Trading-API-only feature as the AddItem/VideoDetails docs might suggest. So the integration surface is much smaller than the P3 implies: the eBay side is three new calls plus one extra field on a payload we already build.

FINDING 2 — THE REAL COST IS TRANSCODING, AND IT LANDS ON AC2. eBay accepts .mp4 MPEG-4 Part 10 / AVC (H.264) only. iPhones have defaulted to HEVC / H.265 since iOS 11 unless the user changed Camera > Formats to 'Most Compatible'. AC2 specifically promises iOS compose. So the single most likely real-world input is a format eBay will not accept, and the failure would surface late — after upload, as PROCESSING_FAILED — which is the worst place to discover it. Whoever picks this up should size the transcode decision FIRST, because it dominates the estimate: client-side transcode, server-side transcode (ffmpeg in the Deno container, which is a real image-size and CPU change on Coolify), or explicit rejection. The eBay calls are the easy part.

FLOW: createVideo returns 201 with the video id in the Location header -> uploadVideo sends the bytes -> poll getVideo. Statuses PENDING_UPLOAD -> PROCESSING -> LIVE, with BLOCKED and PROCESSING_FAILED as the other terminal states. BLOCKED is a moderation verdict rather than a fault, so it needs its own message; a generic retry there loops forever. Rate limit is 50 POSTs / 5s per user.

ALSO: AC3's original wording ('routes through the hardened fetch path') is misleading and has been rewritten. Our upload hardening is image-specific — validateImageUpload magic-byte-sniffs for images and stripImageMetadata drops EXIF/GPS from images. Neither does anything for an .mp4, which carries its own location metadata. Video needs a parallel validator, not a reuse of the image one.

NOT CONFIRMED, flagged rather than guessed: max file size, max duration, and how many videos a single listing accepts. eBay's docs point at Seller Center for those numbers and I could not retrieve them (developer.ebay.com WebFetch timed out twice; the above is from eBay doc search summaries, not the doc pages read directly). Confirm those three numbers against the live docs before implementing, since max-duration in particular shapes the compose UX.

userStories.title: Authenticity tell coverage follows brand-pack order, not counterfeit prevalence
userStories.description: As GradeThread, we want tell coverage driven by what actually gets faked, because an add-on a seller can buy for any brand currently has real depth for three (CANONICAL_TELLS: louisvuitton, coach, gucci) and legacy free-text {tell, detail} rows for the rest, which brand-authenticity.ts coerces to category 'other' with no redFlag and which therefore contribute almost nothing to the verdict. The 37 migrations that mention authentication_tells were written in brand-pack order — luxury first because that pack came first — not from any ranking of counterfeit exposure. Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia are among the most-counterfeited apparel brands in the world and sit in packs whose tells were never structured. US-2139 fixes the SHAPE and the depth of what we have; this story fixes WHICH BRANDS we invest in next and why.
acceptanceCriteria: A written, sourced prioritization of brands by counterfeit exposure crossed with our own submission volume, recorded in the vault as a decision note rather than in a commit message.
The top-ranked brands get structured, sourced, verified tells with redFlags — not free-text rows.

The add-on's purchasability is reconciled with coverage: a brand with no verified tells either cannot be purchased for, or is sold with an explicit stated limitation. Silent degradation to generic reasoning is not acceptable for a paid add-on.
Coverage is measurable: a query or admin view reports verified-tell count per brand so the gap is visible instead of anecdotal.
No claim about detection accuracy is published anywhere until the authenticity golden set (US-2131) can support it.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Authenticity/Coverage] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Coverage today follows brand-pack authoring order, which put luxury first. Nike/adidas/Supreme/BAPE/Moncler/Canada Goose/TNF/Patagonia sit in packs whose tells were never structured. Pairs with US-2139 (shape) — this one is about which brands get invested in next. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED except AC1's sourced ranking and AC2's seeding (both deferred with reasons). Commit 2c95f59, no migration.
THE PREMISE WAS UNDERSTATED, AND THE MEASUREMENT IS THE MAIN RESULT. The story says coverage follows brand-pack authoring order. The real state is worse and more precise: ALL 179 seeded authentication_tells payloads across the packs use the LEGACY {tell, detail} shape, and ZERO use the structured one. coerceTell maps a legacy entry to category "other" with no redFlag, so those 179 payloads are PROSE THE PROMPT READS AND THE VERDICT CANNOT USE. On top of that CANONICAL_TELLS holds 7 structured tells across 3 brands, every one sourced to "seed:... (unverified — review in admin)". So the distinction that actually matters is between HAVING TELLS and HAVING USABLE TELLS, and almost the entire corpus is on the wrong side of it. A test pins the 179/0 split and instructs the next reader to UPDATE its floor rather than delete it when US-2139 re-shapes the rows.
THAT REFRAMED THE STORY. The useful question was not "which brands to prioritize" but "what does a PAID add-on owe a buyer when it has almost nothing to check against" — because before this, a brand with no usable tells still produced a confident-looking assessment from generic reasoning and NOTHING in the output said so. That is the part a buyer would object to, and it needed no new data to fix. AC3 DONE and it is the substance of this commit. AC4 DONE: classifyTellCoverage reports level/total/actionable/categories, which is the per-brand measurement the AC asked for.
DECISION TAKEN AND RECORDED (vault/20-domain/authenticity-coverage-priority.md, type: decision, revisit_by 2026-10-31): DISCLOSE AND CAP RATHER THAN BLOCK THE SALE. Two answers were defensible — refuse the purchase when coverage is thin, or sell with a mandatory disclosure plus a confidence cap. Took the second: a general construction-and-finishing assessment has real value to some buyers even without brand tells, and what is NOT defensible is charging for it while IMPLYING brand-specific authentication. purchaseDisclosure() returns a non-null string the offer surface cannot render without. Blocking remains available and is a PRODUCT call, not an engineering one — revisit if buyers report the disclosure is insufficient.
CAPS: 0.6 with no tells, 0.75 with inert ones, composing by MIN with US-2218's reference cap. Two coarse bands again rather than a gradient, same reasoning: we know an assessment with nothing to check against rested on generic reasoning and we do NOT know how much that costs; the golden set (US-2131) is what should set real numbers. Never raises. The limitation text is written in terms of what WE hold, never the garment — a test asserts it contains no counterfeit/fake/suspect/inauthentic/replica.
ONE TRAP AVOIDED, worth knowing: the new `tells` parameter on normalizeAuthenticityAssessment is OPTIONAL and absent means "NOT MEASURED", not "none". Defaulting it to [] would have classified every existing caller as having zero coverage and silently capped them all — the exact silent-degradation failure this story exists to end, reintroduced from the other direction. A test pins that an existing caller passing no tells is byte-identical.
AC1 DEFERRED, WITH THE REASON WRITTEN DOWN. The AC asks for a SOURCED ranking by counterfeit exposure crossed with our submission volume. Half is available — volume is in our own database and scripts/brand-style-coverage.mjs --db already shows that query's shape. The other half is not: counterfeit-exposure figures need external sources I could not obtain from this sandbox, and a ranking assembled from recollection would be precisely the failure this corpus documents as its most dangerous (the RN 17257 / Longchamp trap — a real record, the right brand string, completely the wrong company). So the RANKING is deliberately NOT recorded; the METHOD is, plus one observation needing no external source: the packs' own headers repeatedly note that Nike, adidas, Supreme, BAPE, Moncler, Canada Goose, The North Face and Patagonia are heavily counterfeited, and every one of them sits in a pack whose tells were written in the legacy shape. That is where the corpus itself points for the first pass.
AC2 DEFERRED (seeding verified tells is the same sourcing project). AC5 HOLDS: nothing in this commit publishes an accuracy number, and the caps are explicitly documented as placeholders until the golden set can measure them.
VERIFICATION: 4703 edge tests pass, 15 new in authenticity-coverage_test.ts; the 8 failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210. deno lint clean; zero new type errors.

userStories.title: Authentication tells are text-only — there is no known-genuine reference imagery to check a font, stitch or stamp against
userStories.description: As a reviewer or a grading model, I want a picture of what genuine looks like, because half our tell taxonomy is VISUAL and cannot be verified from prose. Verified: brand-authenticity.ts defines 11 tell categories including stitching, font, stamp, hardware and construction, and CANONICAL_TELLS's own text admits the gap — the Louis Vuitton stamp tell says to 'compare letter spacing/shape to a KNOWN-GENUINE REFERENCE' and no such reference exists anywhere in the system. A tell whose check instruction depends on an artifact we do not have is not a checkable rule. This is distinct from US-2139 (tell DEPTH and counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks): this is the missing evidence layer both of those assume.
acceptanceCriteria: A reference-image store exists for tells, with per-image provenance (source, rights, brand, style, tell category) — reference imagery must be licensed or owned, never scraped into a public surface.
Reference images are private by default and served only through signed URLs, consistent with the submission-images posture; they are NEVER placed in the public item-photos bucket.

The authenticity pass can present the relevant reference alongside the suspect region for a comparison, and a tell with no reference is explicitly marked as unverifiable-visually rather than silently scored.
Seller-submitted photos are NEVER promoted into the reference corpus without explicit consent — the few-shot exemplar privacy rule (US-1067) applies with equal force here.
Absence of a reference widens limitations and lowers confidence; it must not produce a confident verdict from generic reasoning.
userStories.notes:
[P2][Authenticity/Evidence] [EPIC: Grading Depth US-2209] Filed 2026-07-28 from a deep-dive review of the grading model + grading knowledge base (owner-requested). Distinct from US-2139 (tell depth + counterfeit-side modelling) and US-2138 (decoder cross-checks) — this is the missing EVIDENCE layer both assume. Self-evident from CANONICAL_TELLS's own text: the LV stamp tell instructs a comparison against a known-genuine reference we do not have. | 2026-07-28 SHIPPED (table starts empty; seeding real imagery is the sourcing half). Commit a0fc163, migration 00500 (HELD). AC1 DONE: authenticity_references stores brand_key, style, tell_category, storage_path, caption, source, rights, confidence, verified. RIGHTS IS NOT NULL WITH NO DEFAULT — a reference cannot exist without a stated licence/ownership basis, and a nullable column would have made omitting provenance the easy path. Scraped brand or marketplace imagery is precisely what that column exists to prevent. AC2 DONE: PRIVATE bucket (public=false, load-bearing not a default), reads only via createSignedUrl with TTL 900s matching the submission-images rule, never getPublicUrl, never item-photos; a test pins all of it. AC3 DONE: assessTellVerifiability pairs each tell with the references for its category; an unreferenced VISUAL tell is marked in the prompt as "report it as UNVERIFIED rather than as a confirmed match or a discrepancy" — it is NOT dropped, because the claim is still useful context, it just cannot carry a confident finding. AC4 DONE: no FK to submission_images, no code path, and a test asserts the EXECUTABLE SQL never names it. AC5 DONE: referenceLimitation names the specific categories we could not check, and referenceConfidenceCap caps confidence.
THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS: ABSENCE LOWERS CONFIDENCE, IT NEVER RAISES SUSPICION. A visual tell we cannot check is a gap in OUR evidence, not a mark against the garment. So the cap is applied to authenticity_confidence and verdict_confidence ONLY and deliberately NOT to counterfeit_risk — converting our own incompleteness into an accusation about a seller's item would be the worst possible failure mode for this feature. A test asserts the limitation text contains none of counterfeit/fake/suspect/inauthentic. The cap composes by MIN and can only lower (grading-engine contract).
THE CAP IS TWO COARSE BANDS, NOT A FORMULA (0.6 when no visual tell is referenced, 0.8 when some are). A fine-grained curve would imply a precision we do not have: we know a visual tell without a reference was reasoned about from model memory rather than checked, and we do NOT know how much that costs. Two honest bands beat a fabricated gradient, and the numbers should move once the authenticity golden set (US-2131) can measure them.
ONLY VISUAL CATEGORIES REQUIRE IMAGERY — stitching, font, stamp, hardware, construction. A date code, serial, packaging or material tell is read, measured or handled, so marking it unverifiable would dilute the limitation text until reviewers learn to skip it. That restraint is what keeps the disclosure meaningful.
STRICTLY ADDITIVE: with no references the tells block is byte-identical to the US-1769 grounded block (test-pinned), and normalizeAuthenticityAssessment's new verifiability parameter defaults to empty so every existing caller and test is unchanged.
WHAT IS NOT DONE: the table is EMPTY. Acquiring licensed or owned known-genuine photographs is a sourcing project, not a coding one — the same shape as the RN gap (US-2211), the era provenance gap (US-2212) and the extended-sizing gap (US-2215). Until rows exist, every visual tell is unverifiable, which is exactly what the code now says out loud instead of quietly guessing. Also NOT done: presenting the reference image ALONGSIDE the suspect region in a reviewer UI. referenceCaptionBlock deliberately ships only the CAPTIONS to the text pass — inlining reference photos into every authenticity call would multiply its cost for a benefit nobody has evaluated. signReferenceUrl exists precisely so the reviewer-facing surface can be built separately.
TWO SELF-INFLICTED BUGS, both caught and worth remembering. (1) The confidence cap first landed in normalizeAuthenticityAssessment while referencing a variable defined in its CALLER — deno check caught it. Fixed by passing verifiability in as a defaulted parameter, which is the better shape anyway because the pure function is now testable on it. (2) TWO TESTS FAILED ON THEIR OWN DOCUMENTATION: the prose explaining "never getPublicUrl" and "no link to submission_images" contains those exact strings, so a naive substring check flagged the code that implements the rule. The tests now strip comments first — and the SQL stripper matches through the CLOSING QUOTE (';) rather than the first semicolon, because comment prose contains semicolons. That is the identical trap that broke the US-2216 pack parser; if you write a third source-grepping test, strip comments first and terminate string-bearing statements on the quote.
VERIFICATION: 4688 edge tests pass, 19 new; the 8 failures are the same pre-existing imagescript-FFI / network-timeout sandbox artifacts confirmed against a clean tree in US-2210 (a mid-run count of 15 was my regression and is fixed). deno lint clean; no new type errors. 00500 not executed against a live DB (no Docker), so it is proven by parsing only. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-07-29: the HELD-migration claim above is STALE and should not be acted on. Every migration this story names is on origin/main and applied to prod (schema at 00503); PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is empty and the branch is not frozen.

userStories.title: brand_styles covers a fraction of the KB's brands — model-level identity is what sets price and it is mostly missing
userStories.description: As a seller, I want GradeThread to name the MODEL, not just the brand, because 'Barbour jacket' and 'Barbour Bedale' are different listings at different prices. Verified: 70 migration statements insert into brand_knowledge (about 177 canonical brands) but only 36 insert into brand_styles, and the style rows that exist concentrate on flagship lines. brand_styles already has the right shape for this (style_name, aliases, product_line, department, category, visual_fingerprint, fabric_tech, era, msrp_band, keywords) — it is under-populated, not under-designed. The knock-on is real: without a style row there is no visual_fingerprint for the extractor to disambiguate against, no msrp_band for comping, and no style-level anchor for the condition baseline (see the companion story on garment_baselines).
acceptanceCriteria: Style coverage is prioritized by actual submission and listing volume per brand, not by KB seeding order — name the query that produced the priority list.
Every new style row carries visual_fingerprint and keywords populated (those are what make a style row usable by the extractor), plus source_url and confidence.
A golden-harness case per seeded style asserts the style is recoverable from a representative description/photo-derived field set, extending the existing brand-knowledge-golden_test.ts pattern.
