userStories.title: Substantiation review of every public authenticity claim and its framing
userStories.description: Authenticity verdicts (likely_authentic / inconclusive / red_flags) are shown on public certificates and returned from an unauthenticated public endpoint, currently with no accuracy gate behind them. Separately, the seeded brand KB was written to REFUSE authentication — 00398_coach_brand_knowledge.sql:14 reads 'NEVER auto-authenticate... A creed/serial proves NOTHING about authenticity on its own' — so our own knowledge base contradicts the product's public posture. That contradiction needs resolving deliberately, not by drift.
acceptanceCriteria: Review every user-facing authenticity string against what the evidence can actually support, with counsel — fold into the US-2114 review gate rather than running a separate process.

Decide and document the claim posture: assessment/opinion with stated limitations vs verification. The pipeline is built for the former (confidence ceilinged at 0.9, hard-capped to 0.5 on contradiction, limitations set from a constant the model cannot override) — keep that discipline in the copy.
Reconcile the brand-KB 'never auto-authenticate' guidance with the shipped product posture.

Check eBay policy exposure: grade-badge.ts is already dead because eBay bans grade overlays on listing imagery, and eBay runs its own Authenticity Guarantee — determine what may be stated on a listing before building listing-facing surfaces.
Confirm the unauthenticated public endpoint should expose verdicts at all.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Legal][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Pairs with the FTC Section 5 batch (US-2114..2128) — same substantiation problem, different claim. Do not let an agent draft the claim language. ACCURACY GATE 2026-07-19 (decided: adopt the conservative posture ahead of counsel): the public /tools/authenticity-check endpoint now requires a PASSING eval run in addition to PUBLIC_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK_ENABLED. CORRECTION to an earlier characterisation of the exposure: that endpoint was ALREADY fail-closed behind the env flag (default off) and documented as awaiting legal review of the limitations copy — so the risk was lower than described. What was missing is that the env flag is the LEGAL gate (a human read the copy) and says nothing about whether the model is any good; enabling it after a legal review should not be sufficient to publish verdicts from a prompt version that has never cleared the golden set. The two gates are now separate and both required. Authenticated surfaces (paid add-on, buyer check) deliberately still run ungated — they carry the limitations disclaimer and a named account, a different posture from an anonymous public claim. Returns 503 + Retry-After rather than 404 so a crawler does not deindex the tool page behind it. 4431 edge tests pass. | 2026-08-09 AC3 NOW OWNS A REQUIREMENT THAT WAS DUPLICATED, and inherits the evidence. US-2139 AC6 asked for the same reconciliation ('see US-2133' in its own text) and has been closed as a duplicate, so this AC is the single home for it. WHAT THE CONTRADICTION ACTUALLY IS, measured rather than described, so the work starts from facts: 37 seeded brand packs carry prose such as 'NEVER label a Coach item authentic — flag anything inconsistent in condition notes only' (00398_coach_brand_knowledge.sql) and 'LUXURY — never auto-authenticate' (00399_louis_vuitton_brand_knowledge.sql), while the shipped pipeline's deriveVerdict (lib/ai-authenticity.ts) emits 'likely_authentic' as one of three possible verdicts on a PAID add-on. TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THIS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS. (1) The gap may be one of WORDING rather than of posture: the shipped verdict is confidence-capped (AUTHENTICITY_VERDICT_CONFIDENCE_CEILING 0.9, harder caps for contradictions, no-macro evidence, thin reference coverage and — as of today — unverified brand tells) and carries a mandatory disclosure, so a capped-and-disclosed 'likely authentic' is arguably not the act the KB prose forbids. Settling that is AC2's job and this AC's answer follows from it. (2) THE FIX CANNOT BE AN EDIT TO THE SEEDS. That prose lives in applied migrations, which are immutable — the reconciliation has to land in the vault (vault/20-domain/brands/ already owns the KB's governing rules) with the seeds left alone, exactly as US-2059 requires for any knowledge stranded in a migration header. ⚠ NOT AGENT WORK, restating this story's own instruction because it is the thing most likely to be overlooked by whoever picks it up: 'Do not let an agent draft the claim language', and AC1 requires review WITH COUNSEL. What an agent CAN safely do here is exactly what this note does — locate both sides, quote them, and stop. | 2026-08-10 THE INVENTORY AC1 NEEDS NOW EXISTS, and nothing here drafts a claim. This story's own note says what an agent may safely do - locate both sides, quote them, and stop - and the 2026-08-09 pass did that for ONE example (the brand-KB contradiction). This does it exhaustively, which is the difference between an anecdote and an inventory. NEW vault/20-domain/authenticity-claim-register.md. The three verdicts and the exact strings a user reads; what the pipeline actually supports for them; what the evidence base actually is; and the KB contradiction, carried over rather than restated. THE ONE OBSERVATION WORTH THE WHOLE PAGE: the rendered labels are deliberately WEAKER than the enum names. likely_authentic renders as 'Looks consistent with genuine' - an observation about photographs - where the enum name would read as a judgement about the item. That single string IS the product's legal posture, and nothing was pinning it. A copy edit to 'Authentic' would be a posture change that nobody would file a bug about. It is pinned now. WHAT BACKS THE CLAIMS, gathered so a reviewer is not doing archaeology: AUTHENTICITY_LIMITATIONS is a fixed constant the model cannot author and states in the output that this is 'not a definitive authentication, legal opinion, or guarantee' and 'one trust signal, not proof'; AUTHENTICITY_NO_MACRO_LIMITATION is appended when no close-up backed the read; confidence is ceilinged and capped harder on contradiction, missing macro evidence, thin coverage and unverified tells, composing by minimum and never raising; and the public endpoint has TWO independent gates because the env flag is the LEGAL gate and says nothing about whether the model is any good. AND THE UNCOMFORTABLE NUMBER, because the review needs it more than any of the above: all 179 seeded authentication_tells payloads use the LEGACY {tell, detail} shape and ZERO use the structured one, so coerceTell maps them to category 'other' with no redFlag - they are prose the prompt reads and the verdict cannot use. CANONICAL_TELLS holds 7 structured tells across 3 brands, every one sourced 'unverified - review in admin'. The distinction that matters is between HAVING tells and having USABLE tells (US-2219 measured this; the register carries it forward rather than making the reviewer find it). GUARD: NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/authenticity-claim-register_test.ts. Reads the verdict union from the TYPE and the labels from the page's map, and fails when either is unregistered - so a fourth verdict or a reworded label cannot ship unseen. It also fails a label containing Authentic / Verified / Confirmed genuine / Genuine item / Guaranteed, requires the positive verdict to stay an observation ('consistent'), and fails if AUTHENTICITY_LIMITATIONS stops saying the two things the register cites it for. Plus the same honesty rule as the subscription register: no line may claim substantiation without a dated record. FIVE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the positive verdict reworded to 'Authentic', a label reworded without updating the register, a fourth verdict added, the limitations constant losing 'not proof', and the register claiming substantiation. STILL passes:false and nothing here changes that. AC1 is the review itself, AC2 the posture decision, AC3 the KB reconciliation, AC4 the eBay policy question, AC5 whether the unauthenticated endpoint should expose verdicts at all - all counsel or owner work. What changed is that the review has a complete list with its evidence attached, and the one string carrying the posture can no longer move by accident while it waits. VERIFIED: authenticity-claim-register_test.ts 5 passed (new); deno lint clean across 1490 files; full edge suite 6481 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; vault:lint --strict clean at 168 notes.

userStories.title: Garment sellers are never asked for a serial or date-code photo
userStories.description: photo-profiles.ts:31-45 defines serial and marking slots but surfaces them ONLY for non-clothing profiles. A garment seller is never prompted for a date code, interior stamp, or hardware close-up — while ai-authenticity.ts:142-151 asks the model for stitch-per-inch, embroidery backing, screen-print registration and rivet engraving. acceptanceCriteria: Add serial/date-code and hardware/stamp macro slots to the clothing photo profile, surfaced when the authenticity add-on is active.
Make them optional-but-encouraged rather than blocking a condition grade — a grade must never fail because an authenticity slot was skipped.
Feed slot presence into the authenticity confidence: absent macro evidence should lower confidence and widen limitations, not be silently ignored.
Mirror across web and iOS (photo required-set and order surfaces change together — see the photo-required-and-order-surfaces memory; ~7 spots).
Update the prompt so it asks only for what the available slots can actually support.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Capture][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Highest-leverage unblocked item in Phase 1 — everything downstream depends on capturing the right pixels. PARTIAL 2026-07-19: added optional serial (Serial / Date code) + marking (Brand stamp / Hardware) roles to the CLOTHING photo profile with macro-specific hints. Kept OPTIONAL so a condition grade can never fail on a skipped authenticity slot, which also avoids touching the ~7-surface required-set duplication. STILL OPEN on this story: (a) feed slot presence into authenticity confidence so absent macro evidence lowers it and widens limitations rather than being silently ignored; (b) narrow the prompt so it stops asking for evidence no slot can supply; (c) surface the slots conditionally when the add-on is active. ITER3 2026-07-19: closed the confidence half. (1) FIXED A GAP IN ITER2 — serial/marking were absent from AUTHENTICITY_IMAGE_PRIORITY, so the new slots would have been captured and never reached the model; they now rank ABOVE label so a deliberate authenticity frame is not crowded out of the MAX_AUTHENTICITY_IMAGES budget. (2) hasMacroEvidence() + AUTHENTICITY_NO_MACRO_CONFIDENCE_CAP=0.7 composed into applyVerdictCap as min-of-caps (never raises, per the grading-engine rule); detail deliberately does NOT count as macro evidence. (3) limitations widened with a fixed constant when no macro frame backed the verdict. Image types are taken POST-selection, so a macro frame dropped by the cap cannot license confidence. New params default to the old behavior so existing callers are byte-identical. 4354 edge tests pass (+6). PRODUCT DECISION LEFT OPEN: 0.7 was chosen because it sits exactly on both thresholds — deriveVerdict needs >=0.7 for likely_authentic and authenticityNeedsReview forces review BELOW 0.7 — so it removes high confidence without flipping every existing no-macro verdict to inconclusive or flooding the review queue. Going stricter is defensible but changes the headline verdict on past assessments; that is a product call, not a refactor call. STILL OPEN: narrow the prompt (it still asks for stitch-per-inch/embroidery backing that only a macro frame could support) and surface the slots conditionally when the add-on is active. BLOCKED (prompt half) 2026-07-19: narrowing SYSTEM_PROMPT is a PROMPT TEXT change, and the grading-engine contract requires that to go through shadow -> eval gate -> canary rather than a silent edit. The authenticity eval cannot pass until US-2131 seeds a golden set, so the prompt narrowing is GATED ON US-2131 — it is not independently shippable. Deliberately NOT edited silently. When unblocked, the sanctioned route is the additive/flag-gated pattern the skill describes: a macro-awareness block that suffixes prompt_version (mirroring authenticity_v1+tells) and is byte-identical when disabled, test-guarded. | 2026-08-11 AC1 CLOSED — the slots are now conditional. They had been added to CLOTHING_TAIL unconditionally, so EVERY clothing seller was asked to 'fill the frame with the date code' for an add-on most of them cannot buy. applyAuthenticityMacroVisibility(profile, eligible) is pure and lives in photo-profiles.ts; the eligibility read lives in the route, so the table stays unit-testable with no database. THE FILTER IS SCOPED TO CLOTHING AND THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: serial and marking mean two different things. On a WATCH, HANDBAG, JEWELLERY, ELECTRONICS or COLLECTIBLE they are core CONDITION evidence — jewelry, bags and electronics even mark one REQUIRED — and a watch with no reference number is under-photographed whatever anyone bought. Those five profiles are untouched, test-asserted by name. ELIGIBILITY IS ACCOUNT-LEVEL, NOT THE PER-SUBMISSION OPT-IN, and the distinction is forced by the timing: the add-on is chosen at grade time on a paid tier (routes/grade.ts), which has not happened yet when the capture list is being drawn. So the honest question here is 'could they use these?' — isFeatureEnabled('authenticity_addon', {userId}) — not 'did they buy it?'. FAILS OPEN to the pre-US-2134 behaviour: isFeatureEnabled defaults true on a missing row or read error, which is the right direction, since wrongly showing two optional slots costs a little scrolling while wrongly hiding them means a seller who PAID for the add-on is never asked for its photos. The eligible path returns the SAME OBJECT (assertStrictEquals across every profile), so 'nothing changed for sellers who have the add-on' is checkable rather than asserted. ⚠ THE TENANT-ISOLATION AUDIT FOUND A REAL BUG IN MY FIRST VERSION and it is the reverse of a leak. I wrote 'workspaceOwnerId ?? userId', which is the correct expression — but only authMiddleware was mounted on /api/flipdesk/photo-profiles/*, never workspaceMiddleware, so workspaceOwnerId was ALWAYS undefined and the first half was dead code. authenticity_addon is in PLAN_TARGETABLE_FLAGS, so a member capturing inside owner A's paid workspace would have been judged on their own free plan and lost the slots A paid for — precisely the 'wrongly hiding them' direction my own docstring calls the worse failure. Fixed by mounting workspaceMiddleware (absent header defaults to the caller, so solo users are unaffected); a test asserts the MOUNT, since the route expression was already right and what was missing was the middleware that gives it meaning. AC2 HOLDS AND IS NOW PINNED: a test fails if any clothing authenticity macro is ever marked required, because a hidden required slot would block a condition grade. AC3 was closed in ITER3. FOUR SABOTAGES, each reddening its own case: the clothing scope removed (strips watches), the eligible path returning a copy, only 'serial' filtered with 'marking' forgotten, and workspaceMiddleware unmounted. ⚠ ONE TEST OF MINE FAILED AGAINST CORRECT CODE first run: I filtered non-clothing as 'category !== clothing', but the clothing sub-profiles are keyed clothing:top, clothing:dress and so on, so five clothing profiles landed in the keep-the-macros case. The list is now named explicitly. STILL OPEN: AC5 (narrow the prompt) remains gated on US-2131's golden set. ALSO SURFACED BY THE AUDIT, NOT FIXED, needs its own story: this endpoint stopped being static, and the iOS and Android clients cache it for an hour keyed on PATH ONLY, with no clear on sign-out or workspace switch. Sign out of B and into A within the hour and A sees B's slot list. Staleness rather than disclosure — the body carries no tenant data, only which optional slots show — but the caches were designed when this was static. Web is already correct (queryClient.clear() on both sign-out and workspace switch).

userStories.title: Capture resolution caps out below what authentication needs
userStories.description: Two downscales happen before upload: web at 2400px width (image-utils.ts:350) and iOS at 1600px long edge, q0.75 — explicitly lowered from 2048/0.8 for upload speed (PhotoCompressor.swift:17-24). The server does no further resize, and Claude's own ~1568px normalization is the effective ceiling. A label filling a third of the frame yields roughly 500px of label: enough to OCR a size, nowhere near enough for stitch density, kerning, weave or engraving fidelity. The only real magnification path today is the Forensic add-on's defect zoom (grading-pipeline.ts:130-172), which crops the retained original and upscales to a 320px minimum — but it is keyed to defect bboxes only, never to tags or hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: Retain a higher-resolution original for authenticity macro slots, or upload them at a higher cap than general condition photos.
Generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching) rather than defect bboxes only — this is the most reusable existing asset.
Measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it, so confidence can be conditioned on real evidence quality rather than assumed.
Respect the existing storage/upload hardening path (validateImageUpload -> stripImageMetadata -> upload) and the Vision budget ceiling.
Do not raise resolution globally — the upload-speed tradeoff that motivated the iOS reduction is real; scope the increase to authenticity slots.
userStories.notes: [P1][Authenticity/Capture][EPIC: Visual Authenticity] Found 2026-07-19 by the authenticity deep-dive audit. STRATEGY CONTEXT: Certilogo was the starting reference, but its model does not transfer — it verifies a brand-issued CLG code / QR on a security label sewn in at manufacture (its AI image recognition authenticates the TAG and detects cloned codes, not the garment's construction). GradeThread inspects garments it never manufactured, with no token. The transferable play is visual authentication of the garment itself, anchored on evidence we can actually capture. Note the scaffolding is ~80% built (ai-authenticity.ts is live in production) while the evidence base is ~5% — this epic closes that gap in order: contain what is already live, then raise evidence quality, then productize the claim. Without this the prompt is asking for evidence the pixels cannot carry, which is precisely how an ungated model produces confident nonsense. | 2026-07-31 AC1+AC5 DONE (web). Authenticity slots (serial/marking/surface/corner/sole) now compress to 3600px, tag/label/detail/defect/interior/certificate to 3000, everything else keeps the unchanged 2400 default -- uploadMaxWidthFor() in src/lib/macro-photo-quality.ts, applied at both upload paths (submission photo-upload.tsx and FlipDesk photo-uploader.tsx). AC5 respected literally: the increase is scoped, because the iOS cap was LOWERED to 1600px deliberately for upload speed and that tradeoff is real on mobile data. STATED PLAINLY IN THE CODE, because the number looks like a win it is not: Claude normalizes long edge to ~1568px, so more pixels do NOT change what the model sees today. What changes is what we RETAINED -- the crop-and-zoom pipeline of AC2 cannot recover detail thrown away at capture, so AC1 necessarily lands before AC2 and looks inert until it does. SIZED AGAINST THE CEILING RATHER THAN PICKED: client MAX_FILE_SIZE and edge DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES both cap at 10MB and the server dimension guard at 12,000px; a 3600px WebP at q0.85 runs 1-3MB, while the ~4700px a third-frame crop would need to reach Claude's own ceiling does not fit -- which is why 3600 and not more. The cap table lives beside the US-2136 QUALITY table on purpose and a test pins that every gated slot's cap exceeds its own floor: a slot with a 900px floor and the 2400 default cap would have been nagged for resolution the pipeline was never asked to keep. Both upload paths now resolve the slot photo_type ONCE and feed both the cap and the gate, so they cannot disagree about which slot a photo is. 32 tests total in macro-photo-quality.test.ts. STILL OPEN: AC2 (generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop to authenticity regions) is edge-side and substantial; AC3 (record delivered pixel density per region) needs per-photo persistence, i.e. a migration, which the held-migration rule bars from being pushed without an operator prod-apply first; AC4 was already satisfied (the storage hardening path is untouched -- this only changes a client-side compress cap). iOS half (PhotoCompressor 1600px) NOT done: Swift cannot be built in this environment. Verified: tsc -b clean, lint 0 errors, 2903 tests pass, build green. | 2026-08-09 AC2 SCOPED, NOT STARTED, and the scoping changes which existing mechanism it should reuse. AC2 says 'generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline to authenticity regions (tag, stamp, hardware, stitching)'. THE DEFECT ZOOM IS THE WRONG PARENT. It exists because a sub-3mm hole on a WHOLE-GARMENT shot falls below a pixel after the vision API downscales, so it crops a bbox out of the high-res original and re-reads just that region. Authenticity macro slots are not that case: serial, marking, surface, corner and sole are ALREADY dedicated close-ups, and they have no bbox because the whole photo IS the region. THE RIGHT PARENT IS ALREADY IN THE FILE, twelve lines below the defect zoom: ai-grading.ts's RereadCandidate / selectLabelsForReread (US-1296) re-reads the retained high-res ORIGINAL of the SAME image with the EXISTING per-image prompt — no crop, no bbox, and crucially no prompt-version change, because the prompt is unchanged. Its own header already names the two regions it covers (an illegible care label, a possibly-manipulated image) and says they differ from the defect zoom precisely because 'the whole label/photo IS the region'. Authenticity macros are a third instance of that same shape, not of the crop shape. THE SELECTOR IS ALSO ALREADY BUILT, as of today. selectLabelsForReread picks on a semantic signal (the pass judged the label illegible, or returned no fiber_content). For an authenticity macro the equivalent signal is now PERSISTED: US-2136 AC4 landed submission_images.quality_score (migration 00568, HELD), the normalized 0..1 sharpness measured on the compressed bytes, and a soft macro is exactly 'worth re-reading at higher resolution'. So the selector is a threshold on a number that already exists rather than a new measurement — which also means AC3 ('measure the delivered pixel density per macro region and record it') is PARTLY DONE by 00568 and should be re-read before being re-implemented: sharpness is recorded per image, pixel density per REGION is not, and for a dedicated macro slot those are close to the same question. TWO PRECONDITIONS THE AC DOES NOT MENTION. (1) The re-read path reads the RETAINED HIGH-RES ORIGINAL, and retention is gated by RETAIN_ORIGINAL_IMAGES — with it off there is no higher-resolution copy to re-read and the whole feature is inert, exactly as AC1 was inert until AC2. (2) The authenticity pass runs INSIDE withImageBufferSlot in parallel with the per-image pass, so a re-read that depends on the authenticity result has the same ordering problem US-2138 hit: it cannot be chained without serialising two vision calls on the paid path. Reading the quality score instead of the authenticity verdict avoids that entirely, because the score is already on the row before the slot opens — which is the strongest argument for the selector above. WHY I DID NOT SHIP THE SELECTOR ALONE: a pure function with no caller is the exact shipped-but-unwired shape this repo has found five times today, and adding a sixth deliberately would be worse than leaving the work scoped. Wire it and the selector together or not at all. | 2026-08-09 (second pass) AC2 SHIPPED, wired end to end rather than left as a selector with no caller. NEW selectMacrosForReread in ai-grading.ts plus its consumer loop in runRereadPass, so a soft authenticity macro now earns a high-resolution re-read of the retained original. IT JOINED THE WRONG FAMILY ON PURPOSE — the AC says 'generalize the Forensic defect-zoom crop pipeline', and it does not. The defect zoom crops a bbox because a sub-3mm hole on a WHOLE-GARMENT shot falls below a pixel after the vision API downscales. A serial, a heat stamp, a corner is already a dedicated close-up: there is no bbox because the whole photo IS the region, which is exactly what the US-1296 label re-read says about itself twelve lines below the zoom in the same file. So this is the third member of the RE-READ family, and it inherits the property that matters — same image, same prompt, so no prompt_version moves and there is nothing to shadow, eval or canary. THE SELECTOR IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A MODEL OPINION, and that is the design rather than a convenience. Its two siblings pick on what the first pass SAID (the label was illegible; the photo looked manipulated). This one picks on submission_images.quality_score — the normalized 0..1 sharpness measured client-side on the compressed bytes, which US-2136 AC4 persisted earlier today (migration 00568, HELD). That is the only signal that WORKS here: keying off the authenticity verdict would mean chaining the re-read behind the authenticity call, which runs in PARALLEL with the per-image pass inside the memory gate, so it would serialise two vision calls on the paid grading path. The score is already on the row before any of that starts. A NULL SCORE DOES NOT SELECT, and the check is typeof rather than Number()+isFinite: Number(null) is 0 and finite, so the naive version would read every pre-00568 image as maximally soft and buy a vision call per macro on every legacy submission. Same coercion trap that produced a fake -9 factor delta in US-2443 this morning; third time today it was caught by writing the test first. MERGED THROUGH mergeAuthenticityReread, the SAME one-directional merge the flagged-photo path uses, and deliberately not a new one: a sharper look at a serial may corroborate a tell but must never launder one away. A re-read is precisely the moment someone would relax 'when in doubt, LESS confident, never more' on the grounds that the second look was better evidence — it is better evidence for FINDING something, not for clearing it. Bounded at 2 by default and deduped by slot; rereadImage is already cached per image_type, so a macro that is both soft AND flagged costs one extra vision call rather than two. 5 cases in NEW ai-grading_test.ts. AC3 IS NOW PARTLY DONE BY 00568 and should be re-read before being re-implemented: sharpness is recorded per image, pixel density per REGION is not, and for a dedicated macro slot those are close to the same question. ONE PRECONDITION THE AC DOES NOT MENTION, unchanged: the re-read reads the RETAINED high-res original, so with RETAIN_ORIGINAL_IMAGES off it falls back to the stored copy and the pass is inert — the same way AC1 looked inert until AC2 landed. VERIFIED: deno lint + deno check src/main.ts clean, full edge suite 6225 passed / 0 failed, vault:lint --strict clean. | STATUS CORRECTION 2026-08-09 (second half of the day): the HELD-migration claim in this story's notes is now STALE. Migrations 00568 are on origin/main - verified with git ls-tree against a freshly fetched origin/main, not inferred - and the branch has zero unpushed commits. A held migration is by definition unpushed, so the word is no longer merely out of date, it is an active instruction to stop on a branch that is not frozen. Nothing in this story is blocked on a push. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: pushed is not applied. Whether the SQL has been run against prod is an operator fact this checkout cannot observe, and PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md is the file that tracks it. Read that, not this prose. userStories.title: iOS silently omits the entire paid consumer grading path, including the 14-day dispute flow
userStories.description: As a consumer grading on iOS, I want the same journey the web offers. There are TWO independent grading pipelines in the edge: the consumer/certified path (routes/grade.ts:209 /submit, :751 /pay/:id, :837 /status/:id, :1117 /dispute) and the FlipDesk/reseller path (/api/flipdesk/grading/{validate,submit,submissions/:id}). Web implements BOTH (new-submission.tsx:647, bulk-submission.tsx:332, submission-detail.tsx:244). iOS implements ONLY the FlipDesk path — Grading/GradingService.swift:6,55 documents and calls validate -> submit -> GET /submissions/:id — and grepping iOS for grade/pay, grade/status and grade/dispute returns NOTHING. So iOS has no consumer certified-grading submission, no per-grade payment flow, and NO GRADE DISPUTE FLOW at all.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide explicitly whether the consumer grading path belongs on iOS. Nothing in IOS_PARITY_AUDIT.md or the Android plan mentions this omission either way, which is weak evidence it is accidental rather than a product decision — settle it in writing.
If it belongs: implement submit / pay / status / dispute on iOS against routes/grade.ts.

If it does not: document why, and confirm the dispute obligation is discharged some other way — a 14-day dispute window that only one client can exercise is a support and chargeback liability regardless of intent.
Any parity matrix must stop treating 'grading submission' as ONE row; scoring it that way marks iOS complete while the entire paid consumer path is missing.
userStories.notes: [P1][iOS/Parity] Found 2026-07-18 by the cross-platform parity deep dive. Two implementations of the core revenue journey is the highest-value drift surface in the repo, and the mobile client omits the paid half. The dispute gap is the sharpest edge: US-1340 tracks a 14-day dispute window as a real obligation, and a user who graded on iOS has no in-app route to exercise it.

userStories.title: iOS: bulk photo import is strictly serial though a bounded-concurrency helper already exists
userStories.description: Both PHPicker import paths — AutoListerReviewModel.swift:218-243 and PhotoIntakeView.swift:907-923 — are plain serial for loops awaiting per photo: result.loadImage() (I/O; for iCloud-backed photos a NETWORK round trip each), then PhotoCompressor.compressOffMain (CPU), then a detached DHash.compute (CPU, :238-240). Meanwhile PhotoCompressor.compressBatch(_:maxConcurrent:) (PhotoCompressor.swift:64-91) exists for exactly this — bounded concurrency, per-item autoreleasepool, order-preserving — and a grep of the whole ios/ tree shows its ONLY caller is Inventory/PhotosDropHandler.swift:20. Neither high-volume import path uses it.
acceptanceCriteria: Wrap the whole per-photo unit (load + compress + dHash) in the chunked withTaskGroup shape already used correctly three times in this codebase: PhotoCompressor.compressBatch, DisclosureStore.renderAll (Disclosure/DisclosureStore.swift:88-115) and ReconciliationService (:215-242).

Keep concurrency modest (3-4) so only a few full-resolution UIImages are resident — that memory property is why compressBatch was written, and parallelising without it trades a latency win for a jetsam risk.
Preserve input order via the enumerate-and-sort approach at DisclosureStore.swift:106.
userStories.notes:
[P2][iOS/Performance] Found 2026-07-18 by the iOS audit. The dominant cost is loadImage(), not compression: for iCloud-backed photos that is a serialized network fetch per photo, so a 200-photo import is 200 sequential round trips. Symptom: bulk import sits on the spinner for minutes rather than tens of seconds when photos are not local, and it widens the window for the 'still downloading from iCloud' partial-failure path the code already anticipates (:255-259). NOT FIXED HERE — Swift is unbuildable on Windows.

VERIFIED 2026-07-18 — REAL, still open, deliberately NOT fixed blind.

Confirmed at PhotoIntakeView.ingestLibraryPicks (:907): a plain `for result in results` loop awaiting result.loadImage() then compressOffMain per item. Strictly serial, so 200 iCloud-backed photos are 200 sequential network round trips.

Refinement to the story premise: the existing helper CANNOT be applied directly. PhotoCompressor.compressBatch takes [UIImage] — images already in memory — while the bottleneck is loadImage() upstream of it. What compressBatch does provide is the exact PATTERN to copy: a windowed `withTaskGroup(of: (Int, T).self)` writing into a pre-sized results array, which preserves picker order (the loop comment notes order matters for the tray) and bounds residency.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT worth recording, because the obvious implementation is wrong: do NOT load all images first and then call compressBatch. compressBatch own header explains why — it keeps only a few full-resolution UIImages resident so a large drop does not spike memory into a jetsam kill. Loading 200 full-res UIImages up front reintroduces exactly that risk. The correct shape is ONE windowed TaskGroup where each task does loadImage + compress together, so at most maxConcurrent full-res images exist at any moment.

Why not fixed here: this is ~25 lines of NEW concurrent Swift on the bulk-import path, with ordering and memory-residency invariants, and it cannot be compiled or tested on this Windows checkout. That is a different risk class from the one-word LazyHStack change — needs a macOS session.

userStories.title: No price-change notice or consent path on any platform
userStories.description: No code path notifies a user of a price increase before it takes effect. Stripe's price.updated and customer.subscription.updated-with-price-delta are not inspected (webhooks.ts:244-281). On Apple, the ASSN router (lib/appstore/notifications.ts:18-32) does not handle PRICE_INCREASE or DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF — Apple collects price-increase consent natively so this is not a rejection risk, but the server never learns a price change occurred, and an unconsented lapse arrives only as a generic EXPIRED. On Google Play, PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is explicitly a no-op (lib/google-play/rtdn.ts:11,107).
acceptanceCriteria: Notify subscribers in advance of any price increase, stating the old price, new price, effective date and how to cancel first.
Handle Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF so server state reflects platform-side changes.
Decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web (it commonly does under state ARLs) and implement accordingly.
Do not implement a price change of any kind until this exists.
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Billing] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). Currently latent — no price change has been attempted. It becomes a live exposure the moment pricing moves, which makes it cheap to fix now and expensive to fix under deadline. | 2026-07-19 AC2 DONE (mechanism — no counsel). Apple PRICE_INCREASE and DID_CHANGE_RENEWAL_PREF now reach server state. routeNotification gained a THIRD kind of verdict, record_only, distinct from both an entitlement action and 'ignore'. THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT: Apple owns price-increase consent natively, so ACTING on these would be wrong — if the customer refuses, Apple lapses the subscription and we hear EXPIRED. But ignoring them meant that later EXPIRED was uninterpretable: indistinguishable from an ordinary cancellation, with no way to tell that a price change preceded it. Recording without acting is exactly the right posture, and it is the same 'known-ignored vs unexamined' distinction I built for the Stripe switch in US-2128 — the two surfaces had the identical defect. REUSED recordAppstoreEvent rather than hand-rolling the insert: it already namespaces stripe_event_id as appstore:<id> and swallows 23505, so an Apple retry cannot double-record. (My first attempt DID hand-roll it — the helper was 180 lines above and I had not looked. Worth noting because writing the second copy is always easier than finding the first.) 4 tests, including the two that matter: record_only must NOT be an entitlement action (not sub_active, not sub_expired, not revoke), and an unknown type must STILL fail closed to ignore — widening a router is exactly when a permissive default sneaks in. REMAINING, and correctly split: AC1 (notify subscribers in advance of an increase) needs the COPY, which is US-2114's gate — but note the DETECTION half is now free: US-2117's migration 00486 added pricing_plan_revisions, an append-only price history written BY TRIGGER, so 'a price changed' is already a queryable fact rather than something needing new plumbing. AC3 is explicitly a decision ('decide and document whether a price increase requires fresh affirmative consent on the web') and belongs to counsel. AC4 is a CONSTRAINT rather than work — do not ship a price change until AC1/AC3 exist — and is worth keeping visible: the pricing_plans trigger will now record any change, so an accidental one leaves evidence. Google Play PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is still a no-op (rtdn.ts) and is the same shape as the Apple fix if someone wants symmetry. Verified: edge 4310 passed, deno check + lint clean. | 2026-07-19 (cont.) AC2 EXTENDED TO GOOGLE PLAY — the symmetry I flagged last pass, and it turned out to be the SHARPER of the two platforms. Apple's PRICE_INCREASE is a notification that a price WILL change; Google's PRICE_CHANGE_CONFIRMED is the user ACCEPTING one. That makes it a consent artifact — exactly what subscription_agreements (US-2117) exists to hold — and dropping it meant the only server-side evidence of the acceptance was the eventual renewal amount, which is an INFERENCE rather than a record. classifyRtdn now returns record_only for type 8, and the reconciler writes an audit row via the existing recordEvent dep (idempotent on the event id) while touching no entitlement: Google owns the consent UI, so acting would pre-empt it, and the next renewal RTDN settles the amount. ADDED A DISTINCT OUTCOME VALUE rather than reusing 'ignored': both leave entitlement untouched, but one wrote an audit row and the other did not. Collapsing them would leave the RTDN log unable to answer 'did we ever learn the user accepted a price change?' — which is the entire point of the branch. TWO THINGS THE TYPE SYSTEM AND AN EXISTING TEST CAUGHT, both of them the system working: (1) adding the union variant broke the route glue's narrowing at `action.productType`, which is TypeScript correctly refusing to let a new action fall through unhandled; (2) an existing test asserted type 8 → ignore and went RED, correctly — it was encoding the old behaviour, and it was right to fail rather than let the change pass silently. Updated it to state WHY 8 left that group, so the next reader sees the reasoning rather than an unexplained gap in [9,10,11]. PROCESS NOTE: this took four attempts because bash ate template literals and regex escapes in inline node -e scripts (the fifth such incident today). Anything containing backticks or regex now goes through the Edit tool, not a shell string. Verified: edge 4312 passed, deno check + lint clean.

userStories.title: Two divergent cancellation paths — the stale portal route bypasses the reviewed flow
userStories.description: The primary cancellation flow is good and should be preserved: self-serve, ~4 clicks / 2 screens, no email or phone required, period-end timing stated on every screen (cancel-subscription-dialog.tsx:106,178,219), a required acknowledgement checkbox, clearly-labelled escape buttons, and an 'Undo cancel' banner afterwards (billing.tsx:373-395). It has one retention interstitial with two off-ramps ('Pause instead' / 'Switch to cheaper plan'), which is defensible but is the part most worth a second look. The defect is a SECOND path: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker routes to the Stripe billing portal instead (flipdesk-plan-picker-dialog.tsx:393-406), with a stale comment 'until US-216's cancel flow ships' — US-216 has shipped. That path bypasses the reviewed dialog and shows different, portal-native copy.
acceptanceCriteria: Route the Free-tile selection through the reviewed cancellation dialog; remove the stale portal path and its comment.
Audit for any other route to cancellation and ensure all converge on one reviewed flow.
Have the review gate assess the retention interstitial against 'simple mechanism' expectations — in particular whether two deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible.
Confirm cancellation is available in the same medium as signup for every purchase path (web-purchased cancels on web; IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet).
userStories.notes: [P2][Compliance/Web] Found 2026-07-18 by the subscription-compliance deep-dive audit. LEGAL CONTEXT (verified 2026-07-18, not legal advice): the FTC's 2024 'Click-to-Cancel' Negative Option Rule was VACATED by the Eighth Circuit on 2025-07-08 and is not in force. The FTC restarted rulemaking with an ANPRM on 2026-03-11 (comments closed 2026-04-13), so a successor rule is in flux. The binding obligations today are (a) ROSCA 15 U.S.C. 8403 and FTC Act Section 5, both actively enforced, and (b) STATE automatic-renewal laws — most importantly California's ARL as amended by AB 2863, effective 2025-07-01, which is stricter than what we do today and expressly covers free trials. Design to the California standard: it is the binding one, and it closely tracks the vacated federal rule, so building to it also front-runs the successor. Every story in this batch needs counsel sign-off before copy ships (see the review-gate story). California AB 2863 requires cancellation through the same medium used for the original transaction. Web is fine; the divergent path is the risk, not the flow itself. | 2026-07-19 AC1 + AC2 DONE (no counsel needed — this half is a code defect, not copy). AC1: selecting the Free tile in the plan picker now routes to the REVIEWED cancellation dialog instead of opening the Stripe billing portal. The portal path skipped everything the reviewed flow was designed for: the period-end statement on every screen, the required acknowledgement checkbox, the reason capture, and the undo banner. A divergent second route is how an audited flow stops being the one users actually hit. THE DESIGN POINT: it is a CALLBACK (onRequestCancel), not a self-rendered dialog, because CancelSubscriptionDialog ALREADY opens this picker as its 'switch to a cheaper plan' off-ramp — rendering the cancel dialog inside the picker would have made the two mutually recursive. The parent owns the flow; the picker only reports intent. When the prop is omitted (i.e. the picker was opened FROM the cancel dialog) the Free tile simply closes the picker, returning the user to the cancel flow they are already in rather than stacking a second copy of it. AC2 AUDITED: after the fix, every remaining portal.mutate() call site is legitimate and NOT cancellation — the plan picker's own non-cancel branch (same-tier interval change) and past-due-banner's 'update payment method'. Using the portal is fine; routing a CANCELLATION through it is not, because cancellation is the flow carrying the review requirements. 4 guard tests pin that distinction explicitly, including one asserting past-due-banner may keep its portal call, so a future reader does not 'fix' it by mistake. The strongest assertion is ordering: the isCancelToFree branch must come BEFORE portal.mutate() AND must return — a guard that merely EXISTS while falling through would leave the bug intact while looking fixed. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED by deleting the guard: that test goes red. STILL OPEN: AC3 (have the review gate assess whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations) is explicitly a US-2114 counsel-review item, not an engineering call — the story itself routes it there. AC4 (cancellation available in the same medium as signup) is stated in the story as already satisfied — web-purchased cancels on web, IAP correctly defers to the platform via .manageSubscriptionsSheet — and I did not re-derive it. Verified: tsc clean, lint 0 errors, web 2293 passed. | 2026-08-03 AC4 VERIFIED — and it was NOT satisfied. No migration. The note said AC4 was 'stated in the story as already satisfied', i.e. taken on the audit's word and never checked. Checking it found a real defect on the server. THE WEB AND iOS HALVES DID HOLD: src/pages/billing.tsx computes isAppstoreManaged and hides every Stripe subscription CTA behind it, showing 'Manage this plan in the GradeThread iOS app' instead; iOS presents .manageSubscriptionsSheet in PaywallView and PlanSection and never calls the web cancel endpoint. THE SERVER HALF DID NOT. appstoreSubscriptionBlocksStripe guarded the SUBSCRIBE and CHANGE-PLAN endpoints and not CANCEL. An App Store subscriber has no flipdesk_subscription_id, so POST /flipdesk/cancel fell straight through to 'No subscription to cancel' — a 400 telling a paying customer they have nothing while Apple carried on billing them monthly. Someone who believes that message reasonably concludes they are not subscribed, and the next thing they hear is a renewal receipt. That is worse than an error: it is a confident wrong answer on a billing question. HIDING A BUTTON IS NOT ENFORCEMENT, which is why the UI half passing did not make AC4 true. The endpoint is reachable from any client holding a token, and the iOS app talks to the same API. FIXED: cancel now returns the same 409 + `action` contract the purchase paths already use (manage_in_app / manage_in_play), which the clients already branch on. Apple and Google both REQUIRE cancellation on-platform, so the honest answer is not an error at all — it is where to go. ORDERING IS THE DEFECT, NOT PRESENCE, and the guard says so: both checks can exist and the wrong one still win, because an in-app subscriber has no Stripe subscription id. A case pins that the medium check runs BEFORE the no-subscription check. 6 new cases in cancel-medium-parity_test.ts: the precedence helpers still recognise active/trialing/past_due on both stores AND still return false for Stripe (or web cancellation breaks for the people it is for), the cancel route refuses and names where to go, the ordering, the purchase paths keep their own guards (cancel and purchase have to agree about who is in-app managed — this story is about them drifting apart once), the billing page still hides the CTAs, and iOS still defers to the platform sheet without calling the web endpoint. ⚠ MY OWN GUARD MATCHED ITS OWN COMMENT, fourth time this session: the ordering case searched for the string 'No subscription to cancel', which the comment above the fix QUOTES to explain the bug — and that comment sits before the guard, so the scan reported the ordering as still broken. Comments are stripped now. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED FIVE WAYS: the cancel guard removed, the guard moved after the no-subscription check, the refusal losing its action, a trialing in-app subscriber no longer recognised, and the billing page showing Stripe CTAs. Each reddened. (One mutation initially reported a false pass because .replace hit the SUBSCRIBE handler's occurrence first — re-run scoped to the cancel handler, where it reddens correctly.) REMAINING: AC3 only — whether TWO deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible under 'simple mechanism' expectations. That is explicitly a US-2114 counsel item, not an engineering call. VERIFIED: full edge suite 5400 passed / 0 failed, deno check + lint clean across 1345 files. | 2026-08-10 AC2's AUDIT MISSED A ROUTE, and it is the one the buyer product exposes. The 2026-07-19 pass concluded 'every remaining portal.mutate() call site is legitimate and NOT cancellation - the plan picker's own non-cancel branch and past-due-banner's update payment method'. It did not include src/pages/buyer/billing.tsx, which renders a 'Manage in Stripe' button. That is a third call site and it was not examined. WHAT I FIXED, because it is unambiguous and in code: POST /portal hardcoded return_url to the SELLER billing page. So a buyer clicking Manage in Stripe was sent to Stripe and returned to /dashboard/billing - a page showing a FlipDesk plan they may not hold, with no way to manage the buyer subscription they just went to change, and no other route back. The eighth instance today of a control built for the seller product and reused for the buyer one without asking whether its destination still made sense. return_url now resolves through renewalNoticeCopy, so 'the page that manages this product' has ONE definition shared with all six billing emails. The route takes an optional product hint; ABSENT MEANS FLIPDESK, so every historical caller is byte-identical, and a body-less request still works rather than 400ing. Tests pin the default, the catch, and that the buyer page passes 'buyer'. ⚠ WHAT I DID NOT FIX, AND IT IS THE BIGGER HALF OF AC2: billingPortal.sessions.create is called with NO `configuration`, so Stripe applies the ACCOUNT DEFAULT portal configuration. Whether 'Cancel subscription' is enabled there is a Stripe Dashboard setting this checkout cannot observe. If it is on - and Stripe enables it by default in most setups - then the portal IS a second cancellation path, reachable from the seller billing page, the plan picker and the buyer page, bypassing the reviewed dialog entirely: no period-end statement on every screen, no acknowledgement checkbox, no reason capture, no undo banner. That is EXACTLY the defect AC1 fixed for the Free tile, still live through a different door, and AC2 asks for precisely this audit. AN OPERATOR CAN SETTLE IT IN A MINUTE: Stripe Dashboard -> Settings -> Billing -> Customer portal -> Cancellations. If cancellation is enabled there, either disable it (the portal stays useful for payment methods and invoices, which is what past-due-banner and the interval-switch branch actually need) or pass an explicit `configuration` id here that has it off. I did not guess: passing a configuration id that does not exist would 500 every portal open, and disabling a feature I cannot see the current state of is not a change to make blind. FIVE SABOTAGE MUTATIONS, each reddening its own case: the return URL re-hardcoded, the default flipped to buyer (which would strand every seller instead), the body-less catch removed, the hook accepting the product and not sending it, and the buyer page dropping its argument. STILL passes:false. AC2 is now HALF done - the return-path defect is fixed and the portal-cancellation question is stated precisely with the exact setting to check, but it needs a human with the Stripe Dashboard. AC3 (whether two deflection off-ramps before the confirm step is defensible) remains a US-2114 counsel item. AC1 and AC4 unchanged. VERIFIED: deno check clean on payments.ts; deno lint clean across 1491 files; billing-portal-return_test.ts 3 passed (new); full edge suite 6484 passed / 0 failed / 176 ignored; npx tsc -b clean; eslint 0 errors / 13 warnings; full web suite 3930 passed / 0 failed across 322 files.

userStories.title: Android has no purchase capability but the server will entitle it — build disclosure in before billing ships
userStories.description: There is no billing package, no BillingClient dependency, no paywall, no disclosure copy and no restore path anywhere in android/ (android/README.md:38 lists billing as planned). Meanwhile the entire server side is built and live: lib/google-play/{verify,rtdn,products,expiry-sweep}.ts, routes/google-play.ts, migrations 00321/00353/00354 — so POST /verify (google-play.ts:108) would grant a real entitlement. Separately, decideAppstorePrecedence (lib/appstore/precedence.ts:30-34) treats a user as Stripe-active only when billing_source is null or 'stripe', and appstoreSubscriptionBlocksStripe (:48-55) checks only 'appstore' — Google Play appears in NEITHER guard, so a Play subscriber could stack an App Store or Stripe subscription and be double-charged.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Google Play to the cross-platform precedence matrix on both sides BEFORE any Android billing client ships.
When the Android paywall is built, carry the full disclosure set from the start — model it on PaywallView.swift:303 rather than writing new copy.
Include a restore/entitlement-recovery path and a link to the Play subscription-management screen.
Add an Android equivalent of the iap-catalog-drift test, including blurb/title comparison.
Until the client ships, confirm /verify cannot be exercised by a client that cannot produce a valid purchase token.
