userStories.title: users_billing_source_chk rejects 'googleplay' — Play subscriptions may be failing outright
userStories.description: 00104_appstore_billing.sql:25 defines users_billing_source_chk allowing only 'stripe' and 'appstore'. The Google Play verification path writes 'googleplay'. If the constraint is live in prod as written, every Play subscription write fails: the customer is charged by Google and receives no entitlement.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm against prod whether the constraint still excludes 'googleplay' and whether any Play purchase has ever succeeded.
Migration extends the allowed set to include every billing source the code actually writes.
A test asserts the constraint's allowed set matches the set of literals the code writes.
If any customer was charged by Google without receiving entitlement, reconcile and grant retroactively.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Android] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Verify against prod before assuming customers were affected — the constraint may have been altered outside migrations. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED, and it is worse than 'may be failing' — it fails, deterministically. users_billing_source_chk is created ONCE, in 00104_appstore_billing.sql line 25: CHECK (billing_source IS NULL OR billing_source IN ('stripe','appstore')). grep across every file in supabase/migrations returns exactly two hits for the constraint name, both in 00104 (the IF NOT EXISTS probe and the ADD CONSTRAINT). NO migration ever drops or re-adds it. 00321_google_play_billing.sql touches public.users but only to add columns — its own header comment says "billing_source already carries 'stripe'/'appstore'; Play sets 'googleplay'", which reads as if the constraint had been widened, and it never was. Meanwhile the Play grant path genuinely stamps it: services/edge-functions/src/lib/google-play/products.ts declares billing_source: 'googleplay' as a literal type on the users update, and the expiry sweep queries .eq('billing_source','googleplay'). So every Play subscription grant UPDATE violates the check and returns 23514, and the sweep can never match a row because no row can hold that value. WHAT MAKES THIS EASY TO MISS: three OTHER constraints were correctly widened for Play — 00354 added 'googleplay' to the dead-letter provider check, 00414 allows it on buyer_billing_source, 00486 allows 'google_play' on the agreed-terms source. Only the seller-side users constraint was left behind, so a targeted grep for 'googleplay' in migrations returns four confident-looking hits and none of them is the one that matters. THE FIX is a one-line ALTER (drop + re-add with the third value), needing the US-1108 triple. Worth checking prod for stuck Play purchasers before shipping it: they paid Google and were never entitled here. | AC2 + AC3 DONE 2026-08-07, migration 00558 (HELD). RE-VERIFIED FIRST as the note asks, and the 2026-08-04 verification holds exactly: users_billing_source_chk is created ONCE (00104:24-25) allowing only stripe/appstore, grep returns exactly two hits for the name and both are in 00104, and no migration ever drops or re-adds it. The writers are three literals and only three — stripe (routes/webhooks.ts:666), appstore (lib/appstore/reconcile.ts:59), googleplay (lib/google-play/products.ts:104) — confirmed by scanning every object-literal assignment across the edge service, src/ and functions/, not by reading the two files the story names. AC2: 00558 drops and re-adds the constraint with the third value. It uses DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS then ADD rather than 00104s IF NOT EXISTS probe DELIBERATELY: the probe is the reason the stale definition survived every subsequent apply, so repeating it would make this migration a no-op the next time someone widens the set. AC3: NEW src/test/billing-source-constraint.test.ts, 3 cases. It does NOT hardcode the allowed set — a constant here would be a THIRD copy needing maintenance, which is the same class of bug the test is for. It parses the live CHECK body out of the highest-numbered migration that defines the constraint (apply order is filename order, so a later re-add supersedes) and compares it against the literals scanned from source. Both directions: a value the code writes that the constraint rejects, and a value the constraint permits that nobody writes. The third case pins googleplay/appstore/stripe by name, because the first two both pass if the Play writer is DELETED and the constraint narrows to match — a silent removal of Android billing rather than a fix. NEGATIVE-VERIFIED: reverting 00558 to the 00104 set reddens 2 of 3 cases and the failure message names lib/google-play/products.ts as the writing file. VERIFIED: tsc -b clean, eslint clean, schema-version_test 18/18 (which is what proves the US-1108 triple — EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION 00558, manifest regenerated to 303 entries, self-record footer present). PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md updated: held count 16 -> 17, and it records that this one is unusual in that it has NO forward dependency — the edge already writes googleplay today and that write is already failing, so applying it makes existing code start working rather than creating a window where old code breaks against new schema. The affected set IS recoverable rather than lost — the Play purchase token is recorded even when the users-row grant failed, so start from the Play purchase records, not from users.billing_source (which by definition can hold no googleplay row). | 2026-08-09 STATUS CORRECTION — THE HELD-MIGRATION CLAIM IN THIS STORY'S NOTES IS STALE. userStories.title: Unlimited free trials: handle_new_user grants 14 days of Pro with no abuse check
userStories.description: 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql:102-104 grants every new signup a 14-day Pro trial with no card, no device fingerprint, no email-domain check and no prior-trial lookup. Deleting the account and signing up again resets it. Each trial can consume real Claude Vision spend.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide the abuse control: card-on-file for trial, per-device/per-email prior-trial record, or a hard cap on trial grading volume. Record the decision.
A prior-trial record survives account deletion (keyed on something that persists, not on the users row).
Trial grading volume is capped independently of the plan's normal allowance.
Measure current exposure first: count trials started vs converted, and grading spend attributable to trial accounts.
userStories.notes: [P0][Payments/Abuse] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Measure before building — the fix depends on whether this is being exploited today. | 2026-08-04 VERIFIED against the LIVE definition, not the one the story cites. handle_new_user has been redefined six times; the current body is 00401_buyer_account_roles.sql, and it grants flipdesk_plan='pro', subscription_status='trialing', trial_ends_at=now()+interval '14 days' to every signup EXCEPT a buyer-only one (v_buyer_only, from a client-supplied account_type of 'buyer'). No prior-trial lookup, no email-domain check, no device or IP signal, ON CONFLICT (id) DO NOTHING — so one auth user is one trial and a second address is a second trial. The claim holds exactly as filed. ONE CORRECTION TO THE STORY'S FRAMING: 00303 is not the live definition, 00401 is, and the difference matters if a fix is written — 00401 already carves out buyer-only signups, so any abuse check has to compose with v_buyer_only rather than wrap the whole grant. A SECOND THING WORTH KNOWING BEFORE FIXING: the whole function body is wrapped in EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS RETURN NEW, deliberately, so a profile-row failure can never abort auth signup. Any abuse check added here inherits that — if it raises, the user still gets an auth account and gets NO profile row at all, which is a worse outcome than an extra trial. The check probably belongs downstream of signup, not inside this trigger. | 2026-08-08 AC4 IS NOW RUNNABLE — the measurement this story insists on doing FIRST is written as §19 of scripts/prod-diagnostics.sql, so it rides along with the other operator reads instead of being a separate ask. AC1 stays open ON PURPOSE: the correct abuse control is a different control if the answer is 'two people did this' than if it is 'two hundred', and the story is right that building before measuring picks one blind. FOUR QUERIES, ALL READ-ONLY. (a) trials started per month vs converted vs still trialing. (b) THE ABUSE SIGNAL: addresses that normalise to the SAME mailbox once a Gmail-style plus-tag and dots are stripped. That is the cheapest possible way to take a second trial, so any stem with n > 1 is one person holding several. It returns COUNTS and nothing else - no addresses, not even the normalised stems - because this output gets pasted around and the rest of the file is deliberately secret-free. (c) what the trials COST: grading submissions made inside the trial window, per account and worst-case, which is the number that decides whether AC3's trial-specific volume cap is worth building at all. (d) whether any of it came from an account since DELETED, which is what makes the delete-and-resignup loop measurable rather than hypothetical. A READING GUIDE SITS UNDER IT, because the numbers alone do not imply the fix: (b) and (d) both zero means the hole is real but unexploited and a plain prior-trial record suffices; (b) above zero means it is already in use and the record has to SURVIVE deletion, which is exactly why AC2 asks for it to be keyed on something outliving the users row. TWO BUGS IN MY OWN SQL, both found by EXECUTING it rather than reading it, and both would have hurt the operator rather than me. (1) I wrote subscription_status NOT IN (..., 'incomplete'). There is no 'incomplete' - the enum is none/trialing/active/past_due/paused/canceled/comp - so on prod that is 22P02 and, under ON_ERROR_STOP, it ABORTS THE WHOLE SESSION partway through, taking the other eighteen sections with it. That is precisely the failure mode this file's own header says it exists to prevent. Rewritten to name the PAID statuses positively (active, comp), which is also the safer shape: an exclusion list silently counts any status added later as a conversion. (2) account_deletion_log records requested_at, not deleted_at. THE REPO'S OWN GUARD CAUGHT A THIRD THING I HAD NOT THOUGHT ABOUT: src/test/prod-diagnostics-safety.test.ts failed because prod-diagnostics-console.sql - the meta-command-free copy for the Supabase SQL editor - was out of sync. Regenerated with scripts/gen-console-diagnostics.mjs and executed separately; both files now run to completion. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not by review: the FULL file and the FULL console copy each ran against a throwaway local stack with ON_ERROR_STOP=1, both exit 0, zero ERROR lines, and §19 returned real rows against the seeded data (3 trial-window submissions across 2 accounts) - so the queries execute and shape correctly, not merely parse. prod-diagnostics-safety 9 passed / 0 failed. STILL OPEN: AC1 (the control, once the numbers are in), AC2 (a prior-trial record surviving deletion), AC3 (a trial-specific volume cap). NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS AC2, because there is a real tension nobody has written down yet: US-2005 PURGES email-keyed rows on account deletion, so a prior-trial record holding an address would be erased by the very deletion it exists to remember. The shape that resolves it already exists in this codebase - email_suppressions is deliberately EXEMPT from that purge on legitimate-interest grounds, for the same reason (forgetting a suppressed address harms the person the erasure protects). A salted hash rather than an address would be stronger still. Do not solve this by quietly adding a table to the purge-exempt list without saying why.

userStories.title: Batch grading re-charges on every retry, up to 5 times for one garment
userStories.description: lib/grading-batch-worker.ts:59-124 and :155-176: gradeBatchItem unconditionally INSERTs a new submission (:66-79) and calls runPaymentPrecedence (:97) on every invocation. runJob reclaims a stale job (:167) and calls it again with no reference to the submission a prior attempt already created and paid for. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS is 240s but a single image's worst case is already 3 attempts x 120s = 360s, so a job can be marked stale while the original pipeline is still running and may still write a valid grade. After GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS (15 min) the reclaim cron starts a second paid attempt. MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS is 5. Result: up to 5 credits debited for one payload, plus duplicate certificates.
acceptanceCriteria: The created submission_id is persisted on the job row BEFORE the charge, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission rather than creating a new one.

Payment is charged at most once per job row, enforced by an idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions (the column and partial unique index already exist at 00216_credit_ledger_admin.sql:35-42 and the grading path never sets it).
Item lease duration exceeds the true worst-case runtime (3 AI attempts x timeout + composite), or the work is made cancellable.
Regression test: a job forced through 3 reclaims debits exactly one credit and produces exactly one certificate.
Audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id, and refund affected customers.
userStories.notes: [P0][Grading/Billing] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. Highest-confidence money bug from the grading audit — the code path is described concretely and matches the reclaim-cron design. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — the double-charge is FIXED at the root (AC1, AC3, AC4); AC2 is defence-in-depth that now needs a migration, and AC5 is an operator action. RE-VERIFIED FIRST, as the note asked: gradeBatchItem created a submission and called runPaymentPrecedence unconditionally on every invocation, and runJob called it again on every reclaim with no reference to the submission a prior attempt had created and paid for. Confirmed the two windows that made it reachable rather than theoretical: GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS was 240s while one garment's worst case is (AI_MAX_RETRIES + 1) x AI_TIMEOUT_MS = 3 x 120s = 360s (ai-config.ts DEFAULTS), so the worker abandoned a pipeline that was still running; and GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS was 360s — EQUAL to that worst case — so the reclaim cron could pick up a job nobody had abandoned. With MAX_GRADE_JOB_ATTEMPTS at 5 that is up to 5 credits and 5 certificates for one garment. AC1 DONE: the submission id is written to the job row IMMEDIATELY after creation and BEFORE any money moves, and a reclaimed job resumes that submission instead of creating another. The ordering is the point — writing it after the charge would leave exactly the window this story is about; writing it before means a container death mid-flight leaves an UNPAID submission, which the resume path declines and starts clean, costing nothing. The fix is deliberately NOT a smarter charge: payment is per-submission, so resuming skips the charge BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by a guard someone has to remember. NEW services/edge-functions/src/lib/paid-submission.ts holds isPaidSubmissionStatus as its own pure module — it is the hinge the whole fix turns on and keeping it out of the worker means it can be tested without booting the grading pipeline. It fails CLOSED on unknown/NULL/unpaid, and the asymmetry is the reason: a false negative re-creates a submission nobody paid for (free), a false positive skips a real charge or resumes a row we do not own. The paid values are the three grade-billing.ts actually writes — included, credits, paid_stripe — read off the source, not guessed. The resume path also re-stamps status=processing (tenant-scoped, mirroring the charging chokepoint's own .eq(user_id)) and records the API usage the abandoned attempt never got to record, exactly once. AC3 DONE: both windows are now DERIVED from the AI budget instead of written down beside it, because two hardcoded numbers that must track a third are two numbers that drift — which is precisely how the lease ended up shorter than the work it was leasing. GRADE_ITEM_TIMEOUT_MS = (getAiMaxRetries()+1) * getAiTimeoutMs() + 90s composite headroom (450s at current defaults, up from 240s); GRADE_JOB_STALE_MS = 1.5x the lease (675s, up from 360s) so a merely-slow worker is never mistaken for a dead one; GRADE_BATCH_STALE_MS is floored above the job window so the batch sweeper cannot fire before its jobs are even reclaimable. The pre-existing assertion (timeout < stale) in grading-batch_test.ts still holds. AC4 DONE: NEW services/edge-functions/src/tests/grading-batch-recharge_test.ts, 6 Deno cases pinning the lease-exceeds-worst-case relationship, the stale margin, the sweeper ordering, the derivation arithmetic (asserted rather than the literal, so raising AI_TIMEOUT_MS keeps it green), and both directions of the paid-status rule. VERIFIED: 20 assertions run against the esbuild-compiled paid-submission module plus the timing arithmetic reproduced independently (old lease 240000 confirmed BELOW the 360000 worst case); all four changed edge files parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: (AC2) the idempotency key on grade_credit_transactions. The column and partial unique index exist (00216:35-42) but the credit debit goes through the debit_grade_credits RPC, so threading a key needs a FUNCTION SIGNATURE CHANGE — a migration, which cannot be pushed from this host under the held-migration rule. It is defence-in-depth behind the root fix, not the fix itself. (AC5) audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers — an operator action; the query is: grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. | [2026-08-01] Migration status correction: 00508 and 00509 were applied to prod on 2026-08-01 (operator-confirmed), and everything else this note calls HELD is already on origin/main. Nothing here is holding the branch. | AC2 DONE 2026-08-03, migration 00516 (HELD). The note above said this needed a function signature change and so a migration, and that is exactly what it took. debit_grade_credits gains a TRAILING p_idempotency_key defaulting to NULL, so every existing 4-arg caller is untouched; the old 4-arg overload is DROPPED in the same file, because leaving it would let those callers silently keep resolving to the pre-idempotency body. When a key is supplied and a ledger row already carries it the function debits nothing and returns the current balance — returning rather than raising on purpose, since the caller intent (this submission is paid for) is already satisfied and an error would make a harmless retry look like a billing failure and push the caller into a checkout it does not need. The edge passes grade-batch-job:{jobId}, keyed on the JOB rather than the submission because the job is what a reclaim re-runs. VERIFIED AGAINST A REAL DATABASE, not by inspection: applied to the local stack and exercised in a rolled-back transaction — the same key three times debits ONCE (10 -> 7 -> 7 -> 7, exactly one ledger row), a different key debits normally, and a call with no key debits every time, which is the assertion that protects the existing callers. Storage needed no migration: 00216 already had the column and its partial unique index, unused. REMAINING: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. That is an operator action; the query is grading_batch_jobs joined to submissions, grouped by job id, having count > 1. Edge suite 5155/0. | 2026-08-09 STATUS CORRECTION — THE 2026-08-03 SEGMENT'S 'migration 00516 (HELD)' IS STALE. 00516 is on origin/main (93f8a4b3) and applied; PENDING_MIGRATIONS.md's held list is 00564-00572 and names none of this story's migrations. Nothing here is blocked on a frozen branch. HOW THIS HID FROM THE GUARD, which is the part worth keeping: prd-lint DOES warn about a stale HELD claim, and it was silent on this story because it tested the whole notes string for a correction — and an EARLIER segment already carried one. So the first correction a story ever records suppressed the warning permanently, including for a HELD claim written after it. Fixed today: the check now resolves by SEGMENT ORDER, mirroring findUnresolvedDeferrals which already did, because notes are append-only and only a correction at or after the LAST held claim can be talking about it. That one change surfaced three hidden cases at once (this story, US-1880 and US-1996). WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is unchanged and is not a migration question: AC5 only — audit prod for submissions sharing a batch job id and refund affected customers. AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 shipped.

userStories.title: The golden-set eval gate never runs in CI and the live prompt versions have no DB row
userStories.description: Two compounding problems. (1) The grading eval appears in none of the 16 files in .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json. The only eval task there is the agent eval, and CI does not call that either. No build, deploy or PR is blocked by golden-set accuracy. runScheduledEval raises alerts and blocks nothing. (2) The code defaults are per_image_v5 and composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63) but the only grading seed migration (00050_grading_self_improvement.sql:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 and composite_v2, and no migration sets is_active. So the live prompts have no row and were never evaluated. (3) The repo contains no golden-set data at all: zero INSERTs into grading_eval_cases, no seed, no fixture. A fresh database has an empty golden set; runEval throws on empty but grading-monitor.ts:287-294 treats zero cases as a clean skip, so an empty set is silent. Net effect: editing prompt text in ai-grading.ts ships straight to customers without ever touching an eval.
acceptanceCriteria: Confirm first, against prod, whether grading_eval_cases has any rows and which ai_prompt_versions rows are active. Record the answer in the story before building.
The golden-set eval runs in CI and fails the build on regression, or the reason it cannot is written down.
Every prompt version the code can use has a DB row with eval results and qualified_model, including the code defaults.
An empty golden set is treated as a hard failure, not a clean skip.
Prompt text in ai-grading.ts cannot ship without a corresponding evaluated version — enforced by a test, not by convention.
EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 (grading-eval.ts:26-29) is reconsidered: on a 1.0-10.0 scale a prompt can be a full grade point off on average and pass.
userStories.notes: [P1][Grading/Lifecycle] [Audit 2026-07-30 module/platform sweep] Reported by an audit agent; the cited line was not independently re-verified in this session — confirm before fixing. The prompt-lifecycle doc reads as if a pipeline gate exists. It does not. Either add one or correct the doc. | PARTIAL 2026-08-01 — ALL FOUR factual claims independently RE-VERIFIED and TRUE; AC4 and AC5 shipped, the doc corrected; AC1/AC2/AC3/AC6 need prod access or a migration and are recorded with why. VERIFICATION (mechanical, not by reading the cited lines): (1) NO CI GATE — the golden-set eval appears in no file under .github/workflows/, no package.json script, not scripts/verify.mjs, not services/edge-functions/deno.json; the only match anywhere in those trees is a mention in scripts/ralph/progress.txt. Nothing blocks a build, PR or deploy on grading accuracy. (2) THE LIVE PROMPTS HAVE NO ROW — code defaults are per_image_v5 / composite_v4 (ai-grading.ts:62-63); the sole seed migration (00050:121-127) inserts per_image_v2 / composite_v2 with is_active false. Scanned EVERY migration touching ai_prompt_versions: neither v5 nor v4 appears. (3) ZERO GOLDEN-SET DATA — no INSERT into grading_eval_cases in any migration. A fresh database starts with an empty set. (4) EMPTY WAS SILENT — grading-monitor.ts runScheduledEval returned skipped_reason "no active eval cases" and moved on. AC4 DONE, and the reasoning matters: an empty set is the accuracy gate being SWITCHED OFF, not "nothing to check". With no cases the eval never runs, so eval_passed is null rather than false and NO other rule in evaluateAlerts fires — the state where no prompt has ever been evaluated, and none can be, produced complete silence from the only component whose job is to notice. evaluateAlerts now raises golden_set_empty at CRITICAL. Deliberately an ALERT rather than a thrown error: throwing would break the monitor cron on a fresh deploy, trading a silent gap for a noisy one and teaching operators to ignore the job. The message names the remedy AND the anti-remedy ("never synthetic") because an operator reading "the set is empty" under pressure will reach for fabricated cases, which makes every future eval meaningless while reading green. Kept DISTINCT from golden_set_shrank: a 40→0 set is both, and collapsing them loses the deliberate-abuse signal US-2037 exists for. AC5 DONE as a PIN rather than a fix, since seeding rows is a migration this host cannot push: a new case reads both prompt-version constants, scans every migration that touches ai_prompt_versions, and asserts the unseeded set equals KNOWN_UNSEEDED_PROMPT_VERSIONS exactly — both ways. So a FURTHER version bump fails until its author seeds a row or amends the declaration, and seeding one without amending also fails. That converts "nobody noticed for four versions" into "you cannot bump a version without deciding". DOC CORRECTED (the story's own closing note asked for exactly this): .claude/skills/grading-engine/references/prompt-lifecycle.md read as if a pipeline gate existed. It now opens with what the gate does NOT cover — no CI gate, code defaults with no DB row — while stating clearly that the part which IS real (activation and canary refusing an un-evaled version, via checkPromptServingEligibility, US-2300) applies only to versions that go through a DB row. VERIFIED: 4 alert assertions plus the seeding scan run against the real tree in Node (no deno on this host) — the scan reports exactly composite_v4 and per_image_v5 as unseeded, matching the declaration; grading-monitor.ts and the test parse clean; frontend 3079 tests pass, tsc -b clean. REMAINING: AC1 (confirm against prod what grading_eval_cases holds and which ai_prompt_versions are active) — operator only, and it should be done BEFORE the rest, as the AC says. AC3 (seed rows for the code defaults) — a migration, push-blocked here. AC2 (eval in CI) — depends on AC1/AC3: a CI eval against an empty golden set would be theatre, and the golden set must grow from REAL human-corrected grades, never fabricated ones, so it cannot be seeded from this host either. AC6 (EVAL_MAX_MAE default of 1.0 lets a prompt be a full grade point off on a 1-10 scale and still pass) — a product judgement about acceptable error, with a real cost either way, and it belongs to the owner rather than to a sandbox.

userStories.title: FlipDesk grading drops the label photo the pipeline still blocks on
userStories.description: flipdesk-grading.ts:83 sets REQUIRED_GRADING_PHOTO_TYPES to front and back only, with a comment claiming the tag shot is covered by the sub-0.75 review path. That premise is false: lib/image-quality.ts:68 still lists label as required with severity 'block' and there is no carve-out at its only call site (grading-pipeline.ts:1859).
