userStories.title: Mobile caches the photo-profile table for an hour keyed on path only, and it stopped being static
userStories.description: Found 2026-08-11 by the tenant-isolation audit of US-2134. GET /api/flipdesk/photo-profiles used to return a constant, so both mobile clients cache it keyed on the PATH alone with a 1h TTL and clear it on nothing. US-2134 made the body per-seller — the clothing authenticity macros are hidden from an account that cannot use the add-on — so the cache key is now missing a dimension it needs. android/.../capture/PhotoProfile.kt:168 fetches with cacheTtlMillis=3_600_000 and EdgeApi.kt:88 keys with cacheKey(path, query); TtlCache.clear() exists at EdgeApi.kt:359 and nothing calls it, SessionScope.signOutWipe passes clearances=emptyList() (SettingsViewModel.kt:287), and switchWorkspace does not clear it either. iOS PhotoProfile.swift:156 guards on a process-lifetime loaded flag plus cacheTTL 3600. Sign out of account B and into account A on the same process within the hour and A is shown B slot list. THIS IS STALENESS, NOT DISCLOSURE — the body carries no tenant data at all, only which optional capture slots appear — which is why it is filed rather than treated as an incident. Web is already correct: queryClient.clear() runs on sign-out (use-auth.ts:232) and on workspace switch (use-workspace.ts:46).
acceptanceCriteria: The photo-profile cache is invalidated on sign-out AND on workspace switch, on both mobile clients — the entitlement belongs to the workspace owner, so switching workspaces changes the correct answer just as signing out does.

Either the cache key carries the account/workspace dimension, or the clear is wired — decide which, and say why. A key that includes the owner is self-healing; a clear depends on every future exit path remembering.
A guard so a per-user response cannot be cached under an account-blind key again: the audit found TtlCache.clear() already existed and had zero callers, which is the shape that made this invisible.
CANNOT BE VERIFIED FROM A WINDOWS CHECKOUT: iOS needs a macOS session and Android CI is the gate. The server side is already correct and needs no change.
userStories.notes: Filed 2026-08-11 out of US-2134 rather than folded into it — it is a client-cache correctness bug on two platforms, not part of making the slots conditional, and it cannot be built or verified here. Severity is deliberately stated as low: nothing tenant-scoped is in the body. The reason it is worth a story anyway is that the ASSUMPTION it rests on (this endpoint is static config) is now false and nothing in either client records that it changed.

userStories.title: Start a Poshmark share run from the phone, or say plainly that you cannot
acceptanceCriteria: Decide and record how a queued share run learns WHICH closet to open, given the extension deliberately does not store the seller's Poshmark handle and will not navigate to a URL that arrived in a message (US-1876)

If the answer is that it cannot, kind=share is removed from EXTENSION_QUEUE_KINDS in services/edge-functions/src/lib/extension-queue.ts and from the table CHECK constraint, so the API stops accepting work nothing will ever run

If the answer is that it can, extension-unified/lister/job-store.js RUNNABLE_QUEUE_KINDS gains 'share', background.js drains it into the US-2482 engagement engine behind that engine's OWN clickwrap, and extension-unified/test/lister-jobs.test.cjs covers it
Either way the seller is never shown a share trigger that queues a row the drain will refuse
userStories.notes: [P2][FlipDesk/Queue] Split out of US-2481 on 2026-08-11. US-2481 AC1 originally said 'publish, delist, share run'; publish and delist ship on both mobile clients, share does not, and the reason is architectural rather than unfinished work. A share run is the US-2482 Poshmark engagement pass. background.js GT_ENGAGE_START (~:1519) refuses unless the ACTIVE TAB already matches cfg.closetUrlPattern, and the extension holds no Poshmark handle by design ('GradeThread's servers see run counts at most, and never a Poshmark page, handle or cookie'). A background drain has no active closet tab and nothing to build one from. The engagement engine also has its own separate clickwrap, accepted IN the extension, which a phone cannot stand in for. Until this is decided, kind=share is accepted by the API and refused by the drain: planDrain puts it in `unsupported` and background.js completes the row with ok:false. That is honest but it is still an API accepting work it cannot do, which is what this story closes one way or the other.
